tables["drug_exposure"]

A run with gpt-5-mini gave four rows (concept names added in italics; drug_type_concept_id is 32858 NLP in every row):

drug_exposure_id drug_concept_id drug_source_value start end route_concept_id sig visit_occurrence_id provider_id 1 1308304 lisinopril 10 MG lisinopril 10 mg 2020-01-01 2025-06-01 4132161 Oral 2 40164929 metformin hydrochloride 500 MG Oral Tablet metformin 500 mg tablet 2025-06-01 2025-06-01 3 46287328 ceftriaxone 1000 MG Injection Ceftriaxone 1 g 2025-06-01 2025-06-01 4171047 Intravenous 900 12 4 19083494 amoxicillin 875 MG amoxicillin 875 mg 2025-06-01 2025-06-07 4132161 Oral 875 mg PO BID for 7 days 900 12

"Consider a statin" is only considered, the penicillin is an allergy and anticoagulation is negated, so none of them is a row. Drug classes such as "antihypertensives" are left out too: the CDM would store them with drug_concept_id = 0.

Kind. Each drug gets a required kind label, which decides the end date and the visit:

Label Means Visit and provider administered Given to the patient, e.g. "ceftriaxone 1 g IV given in the ED" From the note prescribed Started, prescribed or changed in this note, e.g. "start amoxicillin" From the note taking On the patient's medication list, or reported use Left empty: the CDM fills the visit only when the exposure was started in it

Dates. drug_exposure_start_date is the start date the note gives, else the note date. drug_exposure_end_date is required by the CDM; when the note gives none, it is inferred as THEMIS ratified:

  1. the end date the note gives ("until 06/10/2025"), also kept in verbatim_end_date;
  2. the start date + the planned duration - 1 day ("for 7 days" → 2025-06-07);
  3. for a prescribed drug, the start date + 29 days;
  4. for a taking drug, the note date: the last date it is known to be taken. THEMIS has no rule for medication lists, so this is a convention of this definition;
  5. for an administered drug, the start date.

When the note gives only a stop date before the note date ("aspirin stopped on 05/01/2025"), that date is used for both start and end and reported as single_date, rather than a start after the stop.

Route. The optional route label (oral, intravenous, subcutaneous, inhaled, ...) is stored as its standard SNOMED route concept in route_concept_id.

Not filled. The CDM fills days_supply only from a verbatim days supply, never from other fields, so a duration in a note does not go there. quantity, refills, stop_reason and lot_number are left empty, and dose_unit_source_value is a legacy column the CDM plans to deprecate.

Check the coded drugs

drug_concept_id takes standard concepts of the Drug domain. The CDM prefers the most detailed concept the source supports, such as a clinical drug, over an ingredient, so the mention keeps the strength and dose form. A name without detail can be coded too specifically: in one run "Influenza vaccine" was coded as one seasonal formulation, with a score of 0.41. Review low scores with tables.mappings_dataframe().

docs.title: The device_exposure table
docs.text:
The device_exposure table holds the medical devices a patient has or is given: implants (pacemakers, stents, artificial joints), equipment and supplies (crutches, catheters, insulin pumps, CPAP) and materials such as sutures. Each row is one mention of a device, with its standard concept, its dates and the number of devices. The predefined definition follows the CDM conventions for this table; THEMIS has no device conventions.

import asyncio

from aatm.omop import ClinicalNote, OmopExtractionPipeline
from aatm.selectors import OpenAILLMSelector
from aatm.terminology_mapper import TerminologyMapper

mapper = TerminologyMapper(retriever="text-embedding-3-small", selector=OpenAILLMSelector("gpt-5-mini"))
mapper.retriever.top_k = 30

pipeline = OmopExtractionPipeline(
    "device_exposure",
    model_id="openai/gpt-5-mini",
    mapper=mapper,  # codes device names
)
notes = [
    ClinicalNote(
        text=(
            "s/p PCI with 2 drug-eluting stents in 2021. Dual-chamber pacemaker since 2019.\n"
            "Foley catheter inserted today for retention. Walks with crutches.\n"
            "No indwelling lines. Candidate for ICD. Nicotine patch 21 mg daily."
        ),
        person_id=40,
        note_date="2025-06-01",
        visit_occurrence_id=950,
        provider_id=14,
    ),
]
tables = asyncio.run(pipeline(notes))
tables["device_exposure"]

A run with gpt-5-mini gave four rows (concept names added in italics; device_type_concept_id is 32858 NLP in every row):

device_exposure_id device_concept_id device_source_value start end quantity visit_occurrence_id provider_id 1 4131681 Drug eluting stent drug-eluting stents 2021-01-01 2 2 40481477 Dual chamber pulse generator, device Dual-chamber pacemaker 2019-01-01 1 3 40625746 Foley catheter Foley catheter 2025-06-01 1 950 14 4 4251933 Crutch crutches 2025-06-01 1

The PCI is a procedure, the action of placing the stents: only the stents are a device. "No indwelling lines" is negated, the ICD is only considered, and the nicotine patch is a drug, which belongs in drug_exposure. So none of them is a row.

Kind. Each device gets a required kind label:

Label Means Visit and provider placed Implanted, inserted, applied, prescribed or supplied in this encounter, e.g. "Foley catheter inserted today" From the note existing The patient already has or uses it, e.g. "has a pacemaker", "walks with crutches" Left empty: the CDM fills the visit only when the exposure was started in it

Dates. device_exposure_start_date is the date the note gives (e.g. the implant date, "since 2019" → 2019-01-01, reported as imputed_date_parts), else the note date. Unlike drug_exposure, the end date is optional, and the CDM fills it only when the source gives it, so it is never inferred. When the note gives only a removal date ("PICC line removed on 05/20/2025"), it is used for both dates and reported as single_date.

Quantity. The number the note gives ("2 drug-eluting stents"), else 1: the CDM stores 1 when a device exposure exists without a quantity.

Not filled. unique_device_id and production_id (the UDI, rarely written in notes), the unit columns, which the CDM leaves NULL when the source has no unit, and the datetime columns.

Check the coded devices

device_concept_id takes standard concepts of the Device domain. Device names in notes are often short ("CPAP", "brace"), and mapper scores were low even for right answers in our runs, e.g. "left knee brace" → Knee orthosis at 0.31. Review them with tables.mappings_dataframe() before setting a min_score.

docs.title: Processing large datasets
docs.text:
await pipeline(notes) holds every note and row in memory, and a failure partway loses the model calls already made. For a full dataset, use pipeline.run: it reads the notes in chunks, writes each chunk's rows to Parquet files as it goes, and records its progress, so a run that stops can be resumed.

import asyncio
from aatm.omop import OmopExtractionPipeline, OmopRun

pipeline = OmopExtractionPipeline(
    "ecog_performance_status",
    model_id="openai/gpt-5-mini",
    max_concurrency=16,  # notes extracted at once
    cache=True,          # code each distinct text once, across chunks and runs
)
summary = asyncio.run(
    pipeline.run(
        "notes.parquet",               # or .csv, a folder of Parquet files, a DataFrame...
        "output/ecog",
        chunk_size=200,
        columns={"note_text": "text"}, # source column -> ClinicalNote field
    )
)
print(summary)  # notes built, skipped and failed, rows per table, cache hit rate

Sources. A CSV or Parquet file, a folder of Parquet files, a DataFrame, an iterable of ClinicalNote objects or dicts, or a database query:

import sqlite3
from aatm.omop import notes_from_sql

con = sqlite3.connect("cdm.db")  # or a SQLAlchemy engine for other databases
source = notes_from_sql(
    "SELECT note_id, note_text AS text, person_id, note_date, visit_occurrence_id "
    "FROM note WHERE note_date >= '2024-01-01'",
    con,
)
summary = await pipeline.run(source, "output/ecog")

Columns that are not ClinicalNote fields are ignored. Every note needs a unique note_id: it is how a resumed run knows what is done.

Reading the output. Each table, and the provenance, issues and mappings of its rows, is a folder of Parquet files:

run = OmopRun("output/ecog")
run.table("measurement")    # a DataFrame
run.provenance()            # note_id, entity_id and span of each row (table, row_id)
run.issues()
run.mappings()
run.failures()              # notes that could not be extracted or built, and why
run.status()                # {"built": 9850, "failed": 3}
run.dataset("measurement")  # a pyarrow Dataset, to filter without loading it all

DuckDB, Polars and Spark read the folders directly, e.g. SELECT * FROM 'output/ecog/measurement/*.parquet'.

Resuming. Run the same call again. Notes already built are skipped; notes extracted but not yet written are built from their stored extraction result, without another model call. A note that fails (an API error once retries are spent, a result that cannot be built) is recorded with its error and the run goes on; the next run tries it again, up to max_attempts times in all (3 by default).

Changing the mappings. Extraction results are stored apart from the tables (in output/ecog/ledger.db). After editing an omop block, rebuild the tables from them, with no extraction calls:

await pipeline.rebuild("output/ecog")

A run refuses to add rows built with other mappings to an existing folder until you rebuild, and refuses a folder made with other entity definitions or another extractor: use a new folder for those.

Watching a long run. A progress line is logged every log_every seconds (60 by default), when a chunk is done:

Progress: 12,400 of 100,000 notes done (12.4%) in 41m10s, 301 notes/min; about 4h17m left;
12,380 built, 0 skipped, 20 failed; 31,950 LLM calls, 48,210,330 tokens; cost 14.2031;
cache hits 63%

The time left needs the number of notes in the source. It is read from Parquet files, DataFrames and lists; for a CSV file or a query, pass total=. Logs are shown with aatm.logs.configure_logging().

At the end, the summary breaks the run down by stage (extraction, coding and building): notes or texts handled, time, errors, LLM calls and tokens per model. Give your models' prices, per million input and output tokens, to estimate the cost:

summary = await pipeline.run(
    "notes.parquet",
    "output/ecog",
    prices={"openai/gpt-5-mini": (0.25, 2.00)},  # check your provider's current prices
)
summary.stages["extraction"].usage.by_model  # calls and tokens per model
summary.stages["coding"].cost                # coding is the agent's calls, if any
summary.cost

Each run and rebuild also saves its summary as JSON in output/ecog/runs/. The file is updated at every progress line, so you can follow a run from another process, and it is kept with completed: false and the error when a run stops. OmopRun("output/ecog").summaries() reads them back, oldest first.

Batch extraction, about half the price. For a large run that can wait, pass batch=True to extract through the provider's batch endpoint (OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini). Batch jobs cost about 50% of live calls and return within 24 hours, often much sooner:

summary = await pipeline.run(
    "notes.parquet",
    "output/ecog",
    chunk_size=1000,   # one batch job per chunk
    batch=True,
    poll_every=300,    # seconds between status checks
    max_batches=20,    # jobs pending at once
)
OmopRun("output/ecog").batches()  # the jobs: id, status, notes

Only extraction is batched: coding stays live. Each job is recorded in the ledger as soon as it is submitted, so you can stop the run (or lose the machine) while jobs are pending: the next run, with or without batch=True, collects them instead of submitting the notes again. Requests that fail within a job are recorded as failed notes and tried again by the next run, live or in a batch. Batch calls are counted as <model>@batch in the usage, and priced at half the model's price unless prices has an entry for that id. Gemini takes at most about 20 MB of prompts per job: lower chunk_size if it refuses one.

Row ids. The primary keys of a run are derived from the note: note_id * 65536 + n, where n is the position of the mention in the note. The same note gets the same ids in any chunk, after a resume or a rebuild, and in separate runs over parts of a dataset; ids never repeat across tables. They need a 64-bit (BIGINT) column. OmopTableBuilder.build(..., row_ids="note") numbers rows the same way.

Speed and cost

max_concurrency (default 1) sets how many notes are extracted at once; set rate limits to stay under your provider's quota. With cache=True, a text seen in an earlier chunk or run is not coded again. chunk_size bounds memory; larger chunks let the builder group more repeated texts per coding call.

While a chunk is built (coded and written), the next one is extracted, so the slower of the two stages sets the pace. This pays off when coding takes about as long as extraction, e.g. with the agent; without a mapper, building takes milliseconds and extraction is all the time. At most two chunks are in memory. The two stages share the per-minute rate limits, but each gets its own max_concurrency, so up to twice as many calls may be in flight.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: You see Why Fix OMOP vocabulary database not found: .aatm/omop.db. Run aatm init to build it. The vocabulary database is missing, or the script runs from another folder Run aatm init, or pass vocabulary="path/to/omop.db" Concepts not found in the vocabulary: ['LOINC:29463-8'] A typo in a code, or that vocabulary was not downloaded from Athena Check the code on Athena and that its vocabulary was included in aatm init ... is not a standard concept. Coding cache ...: the vocabulary or search index of this coder changed since N results were cached The vocabulary database or index was rebuilt; the old results are no longer used Nothing is wrong; run the aatm cache clear --coder ... it shows to free their space Coding cache ...: changes to the content of ... cannot be detected A retriever whose data the cache cannot fingerprint After rebuilding its index, run aatm cache clear trace shows error: ... and budget_exhausted in usage The agent ran out of tool calls before an answer Raise max_tool_calls, or use a stronger model Every note needs a note_id in a chunked run pipeline.run was given notes without ids Add a unique note_id to every note, e.g. from the note table The omop mappings changed since tables were written to ... An omop block was edited after a run wrote tables to that folder await pipeline.rebuild(output_dir), then run again ... holds results extracted with other entity definitions or another extractor The definitions (other than omop) or the model differ from the folder's run Use a new output folder

docs.title: Current limits
docs.text:
• Only the measurement, observation, condition_occurrence, drug_exposure and device_exposure tables are supported so far.
  • drug_exposure end dates are not inferred from the quantity and daily dose (the second THEMIS rule), and mail-order prescriptions are not told apart from others.
  • condition_start_date falls back to the note date when the note gives no date, which is later than the real onset of long-standing conditions.
  • With the plain mapper, map searches with the extracted text alone: a unit such as mg/dL, which hints at a serum test, is only used by the agent.
  • Mapper scores are not comparable across retrievers and selectors. The agent's score is a self-reported confidence level, not calibrated yet.
  • Units written outside UCUM ("lb", "x10^3/uL", "mEq/L") are not converted before the lookup.
  • Relative dates ("on admission", "after cycle 2") are not resolved: the next source, usually the note date, is used and the issue is reported.

docs.title: CLI Quick Start
docs.text:
This page shows how to use AATM entirely from the command line.

It is focused on the actual CLI workflow exposed by the commads: init, map, and search-ui.

docs.title: What you can do from the CLI
docs.text:
With the CLI, you can:

  • initialize the local environment
  • build the local SQLite vocabulary database
  • build the mapping datasets
  • build the local vector database
  • run terminology mapping jobs
  • launch the interactive search UI

The main commands are:

  • aatm init
  • aatm map
  • aatm search-ui

docs.title: 1. Get your OMOP vocabularies
docs.text:
AATM cannot ship the OMOP vocabularies because several of them have their own licences. You request them from Athena, which has no API for this, so this step is done in the browser:

  1. Log in to Athena and open Download.
  2. Select the vocabularies you need (for example SNOMED, LOINC, RxNorm and UCUM) and accept the licences of the restricted ones.
  3. Click Download vocabularies and name the bundle. Athena emails you a link to a zip file when it is ready, which can take a while.

Then let aatm init do the rest by passing it the link, or the zip if you already downloaded it:

aatm init --vocab-zip "https://athena.ohdsi.org/api/v1/vocabularies/zip/<bundle-id>"
aatm init --vocab-zip ~/Downloads/vocabulary_download_v5_<bundle-id>.zip

With --vocab-zip, aatm init:

  • downloads the bundle into .aatm/downloads (resuming if the connection drops). If Athena returns a login page or the link has expired, it says so: request the bundle again, or download it in your browser and pass the zip's path instead;
  • unpacks it into ./vocabularies, or into --vocab-dir. It asks before overwriting existing files; pass --force to overwrite without asking;
  • checks that the required files (CONCEPT.csv, CONCEPT_RELATIONSHIP.csv, CONCEPT_SYNONYM.csv, VOCABULARY.csv, DOMAIN.csv) are present, and lists the vocabularies and versions in the bundle;
  • adds the CPT4 concept names when the bundle includes CPT4. This needs Java and a UMLS API key, passed with --umls-api-key or the UMLS_API_KEY environment variable. Without a key, CPT4 concepts are kept without names.

docs.title: Using an unpacked directory
docs.text:
If you unpacked the zip yourself, put the CSVs in ./vocabularies, where the CLI looks by default:

./vocabularies

To use another location, pass --vocab-dir or -vd. The CLI validates this path during initialization. In that case, add the CPT4 names yourself by following the readme.txt in the bundle.

docs.title: 2. Run the initialization command
docs.text:
The init command is the main CLI setup workflow.

It does all of the following for you:

  • creates the local .aatm helper directory where the local databases and aatm config files will be stored
  • ensures .aatm is added to .gitignore
  • builds the local OMOP SQLite database
  • lets you choose an embedding model
  • lets you choose the standard vocabularies
  • builds the mapping datasets
  • builds the local vector database

That means you do not need to call Python setup functions manually for the normal setup flow. At the end, you will be ready to run terminology mapping tasks.

docs.title: Simplest setup
docs.text:
aatm init

This uses the default vocab directory and interactively asks you to choose the embedding model, standard vocabularies and other options.

docs.title: Setup with a custom vocab directory
docs.text: aatm init --vocab-dir ./my_vocabularies

docs.title: Setup with an explicit embedding model
docs.text: aatm init --embedding-model embeddinggemma-300M

docs.title: Setup with explicit standard vocabularies
docs.text: aatm init --standard-vocabs LOINC --standard-vocabs SNOMED --standard-vocabs RxNorm

docs.title: Fully explicit setup
docs.text:
aatm init \
  --vocab-dir ./vocabularies \
  --embedding-model embeddinggemma-300M \
  --standard-vocabs LOINC \
  --standard-vocabs SNOMED \
  --standard-vocabs RxNorm

docs.title: 3. Prepare your input CSV
docs.text:
After initialization, prepare the CSV you want to map.

The mapper expects an OMOP-style SOURCE_TO_CONCEPT_MAP input structure, including these columns:

  • source_code
  • source_concept_id
  • source_vocabulary_id
  • source_code_description
  • valid_start_date
  • valid_end_date
  • invalid_reason

Example:

source_code,source_concept_id,source_vocabulary_id,source_code_description,valid_start_date,valid_end_date,invalid_reason
A01,,LOCAL,"Dor no peito",2020-01-01,2099-12-31,
B02,,LOCAL,"Diabetes mellitus tipo 2",2020-01-01,2099-12-31,

docs.title: 4. Run mapping directly from the CLI
docs.text:
The map command runs a terminology mapping task. You can use it in two ways:

  • with a task config file
  • with explicit CLI options

Both paths are supported directly by the CLI implementation.

docs.title: Option A: run from explicit CLI arguments
docs.text:
This is the most direct fully-CLI workflow.

aatm map \
  --input-file data/source_to_concept_map.csv \
  --output-dir output \
  --translator-id empty-translator \
  --retriever-id embeddinggemma-300M \
  --reranker-id bm25-reranker \
  --selector-id first-result-selector \
  --batch-size 100

docs.title: Run a small test job
docs.text:
Use --limit-to when you want to test with only a few rows.

aatm map \
  --input-file data/source_to_concept_map.csv \
  --output-dir output \
  --translator-id empty-translator \
  --retriever-id embeddinggemma-300M \
  --reranker-id bm25-reranker \
  --selector-id first-result-selector \
  --limit-to 20

docs.title: Apply rate limiting
docs.text:
If needed, you can also pass a rate limit:

aatm map \
  --input-file data/source_to_concept_map.csv \
  --output-dir output \
  --translator-id gemini-2.5-flash \
  --retriever-id embeddinggemma-300M \
  --reranker-id bm25-reranker \
  --selector-id first-result-selector \
  --batch-size 50 \
  --rate-limit 100

The CLI accepts all of these options directly.

docs.title: Option B. Run mapping from a config file
docs.text: The other CLI workflow is to store the mapping task in a config file and pass it with --task-config-path or -t.

docs.title: Example command
docs.text:
aatm map --task-config-path task.yaml

When you do this, the CLI loads the task config file and runs the mapping task from it.

docs.title: Example task config
docs.text:
Task config files are supported as .yaml or .json files.

YAMLJSON 
input_file: data/source_to_concept_map.csv
output_dir: output
translator_id: empty-translator
retriever_id: embeddinggemma-300M
reranker_id: bm25-reranker
selector_id: first-result-selector
batch_size: 100
rate_limit: null
limit_to: null

{
  "input_file": "data/source_to_concept_map.csv",
  "output_dir": "output",
  "translator_id": "empty-translator",
  "retriever_id": "embeddinggemma-300M",
  "reranker_id": "bm25-reranker",
  "selector_id": "first-result-selector",
  "batch_size": 100,
  "rate_limit": null,
  "limit_to": null
}

This is useful when you want reproducible runs or reusable task definitions.

docs.title: 5. Launch the search UI from the CLI
docs.text:
You can also launch the Streamlit-based search interface directly from the CLI:

aatm search-ui

The CLI resolves the packaged search_ui.py file and launches it through Streamlit using the current Python interpreter. Streamlit's file watcher is turned off, since it is only needed while editing the UI; set STREAMLIT_SERVER_FILE_WATCHER_TYPE=auto to turn it back on.

Streamlit search UI screenshot.

docs.title: 6. What gets created locally
docs.text:
After a normal CLI setup and mapping workflow, you will typically have local artifacts such as:

.aatm/
├── omop.db
├── datasets/
└── chroma_vector_dbs/

And your mapped output will typically be written to:

output/mapped_source_concepts.csv

The CLI init command is responsible for creating the local helper resources, and the map command runs the terminology mapping workflow.

docs.title: 7. End-to-end CLI example
docs.text: Here is a full CLI-only path.

docs.title: Step 1: initialize
docs.text:
aatm init \
  --vocab-dir ./vocabularies \
  --embedding-model embeddinggemma-300M \
  --standard-vocabs LOINC \
  --standard-vocabs SNOMED \
  --standard-vocabs RxNorm

docs.title: Step 2: run mapping
docs.text:
aatm map \
  --input-file data/source_to_concept_map.csv \
  --output-dir output \
  --translator-id empty-translator \
  --retriever-id embeddinggemma-300M \
  --reranker-id bm25-reranker \
  --selector-id first-result-selector \
  --batch-size 100

docs.title: Step 3: inspect output
docs.text:
ls output

You should see the mapped CSV file there.

docs.title: Step 4: optionally launch the search UI
docs.text: aatm search-ui

docs.title: aatm init says the vocabulary directory does not exist
docs.text:
Make sure your OMOP vocabulary files are present in ./vocabularies, or pass the correct path with:

aatm init --vocab-dir /path/to/vocabularies

The CLI explicitly checks whether the provided directory exists. You can also skip the manual unpacking and pass the bundle with --vocab-zip (see step 1).

docs.title: aatm init --vocab-zip says the link returned a web page or has expired
docs.text: Athena's link needs a valid, recent bundle. Request the bundle again on Athena and use the new link, or open the link in your browser while logged in to Athena, save the zip, and pass its path to --vocab-zip.

docs.title: aatm init --vocab-zip says files already exist
docs.text: The target directory already has vocabulary files. Confirm the overwrite when asked, pass --force, or unpack into another directory with --vocab-dir.

docs.title: aatm init --vocab-zip warns about CPT4
docs.text: The bundle includes CPT4, whose names must be downloaded with your own UMLS licence. Install Java and pass your UMLS API key with --umls-api-key or the UMLS_API_KEY environment variable.

docs.title: aatm init says the embedding model is unsupported
docs.text: Use one of the supported model names listed in this page. The CLI validates the model name before continuing.

docs.title: aatm map says the task config file does not exist
docs.text:
Check the path you passed to:

aatm map --task-config-path task.yaml

The CLI verifies that the config file exists before loading it.

docs.title: Retrieval fails at mapping time
docs.text: Make sure you ran aatm init first and successfully built the local vector database for the retriever you want to use.

docs.title: API-backed components fail
docs.text: Check that your .env file contains the required API keys.

docs.title: Seeing more (or fewer) log messages
docs.text:
Every command accepts a global --log-level option (or -l), placed before the command name. Logs are written to stderr:

aatm --log-level DEBUG map --task-config-path task.yaml

The level can also be set with the AATM_LOG_LEVEL environment variable. It is passed on to aatm serve and aatm search-ui.

docs.title: Output redirected to a file looks garbled or fails
docs.text: The CLI writes UTF-8 to files and pipes (for example aatm serve > server.log), so open such files as UTF-8.

docs.title: Information Extraction Quick Start
docs.text: This page shows how to extract structured information, such as conditions, drugs and their dates, from clinical documents with the AATM information extraction pipeline.

docs.title: What the pipeline does
docs.text:
Given a clinical note and a set of entity definitions (what to extract), the pipeline asks an LLM to find every relevant mention and then validates the answer against the note. Only spans that really exist in the note survive, each with its exact character position, linked to the entity it belongs to.

flowchart LR
    A[Clinical note] --> B[Numbered lines]
    D[Entity definitions] --> C
    B --> C[LLM extraction]
    C --> E[Validation]
    E --> F[Validated entities<br/>+ rejected candidates]
    F --> G[Records view]

The main pieces are:

Piece Where Role EntityDefinitions aatm.data_models.extractors Which entities to extract, loaded from YAML SimpleLLMExtractor aatm.extractors Sends each note to the LLM and validates the output validate_extracted_entity aatm.data_models.extractors Grounds and checks the model output (also usable on its own) EntityValidationResult aatm.data_models.extractors Validated entities, rejected candidates and the records view

The extracted text (for example "Hypertension" or "Furosemide 40 mg") can then be mapped to standard concepts with the terminology mapping pipeline.

docs.title: 1. Requirements
docs.text:
• A model that supports structured outputs, from one of the providers below. Model ids are prefixed with the provider: <provider>/<model name>.
  • The provider's API key in its environment variable (see Environment variables), or passed with api_key=....
Provider model_id example Key Notes OpenAI openai/gpt-5 OPENAI_API_KEY Google Gemini gemini/gemini-3-flash-preview GOOGLE_API_KEY Anthropic anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 ANTHROPIC_API_KEY Install with pip install "aatm[anthropic]" Ollama ollama/llama3.3 none Uses http://localhost:11434/v1 unless base_url is given OpenRouter openrouter/qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b OPENROUTER_API_KEY Any OpenAI-compatible server (vLLM, LM Studio, Together, ...) openai-compatible/<model> api_key=... if needed Requires base_url=... 
extractor = SimpleLLMExtractor(
    model_id="openai-compatible/Qwen/Qwen3-32B",
    base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1",  # e.g. a local vLLM server
    entity_definitions=entity_definitions,
)

Other providers can be added with aatm.llm.register_provider, or by passing any object with an async generate(system=..., user=..., output_type=...) method as llm=....

docs.title: 2. A first extraction
docs.text:
from aatm.data_models.extractors import EntityDefinitions
from aatm.extractors import SimpleLLMExtractor

entity_definitions = EntityDefinitions.from_predefined("condition_occurrence")

extractor = SimpleLLMExtractor(
    model_id="openai/gpt-5",  # or "gemini/...", "anthropic/...", "ollama/...", ...
    entity_definitions=entity_definitions,
)

note = """## Problem list
* Hypertension, diagnosed 2015
* Type 2 diabetes mellitus and CKD stage 3, both diagnosed 2019

## Assessment
Hypertension worsened since March 2026."""

results = await extractor([note])  # one result per note, in the same order
result = results[0]

for entity in result.validated_entities:
    print(entity.id, entity.key, repr(entity.text), entity.line, entity.start, entity.end, entity.parents)

The extractor is asynchronous. In a notebook you can await it directly; in a script, wrap the call:

import asyncio

results = asyncio.run(extractor([note]))

Several notes can be passed at once and are extracted concurrently:

results = await extractor(list_of_notes)

docs.title: Rate limits and retries (optional)
docs.text:
By default AATM sets no limits. All the notes you pass are sent to the model at the same time, and calls run as fast as the provider accepts them. That is fine for a handful of notes. For larger batches, or a provider with a tight quota, you can set limits yourself; nothing else needs to change.

Limits are set once per process with aatm.llm.set_rate_limits, and apply to every LLM call AATM makes for that model: extraction, the concept search agent and the LLM selectors share one budget per model.

from aatm.llm import set_rate_limits

# Every model: at most 16 calls in flight.
set_rate_limits("*", max_concurrency=16)

# Every Anthropic model: stay under the account's quota.
set_rate_limits("anthropic", requests_per_minute=1000, tokens_per_minute=400_000)

# One model.
set_rate_limits("openai/gpt-5-mini", max_concurrency=64)
Field Default Meaning max_concurrency None (no limit) Calls in flight at the same time requests_per_minute None (no limit) Calls started in any 60-second window tokens_per_minute None (no limit) Input and output tokens in any 60-second window max_retries 6 Retries after a rate-limit or transient error; 0 turns retries off initial_backoff 1.0 Upper bound, in seconds, of the first retry's random wait; doubles each retry max_backoff 60.0 Cap, in seconds, of the wait between retries

The key is a model id ("openai/gpt-5-mini"), a provider ("openai") or "*" for every model; the most specific one that is set applies. Each model keeps its own counters, even when its limits come from the provider or "*" entry. Fields left out take the defaults above. Use get_rate_limits("openai/gpt-5-mini") to see what applies to a model, and reset_rate_limits() to go back to no limits.

The token limit is approximate: a call reserves an estimate of its prompt (about 4 characters per token) before it starts, and the provider's count replaces it when the call returns.

Retries are on even without limits. Rate-limit errors (429), server errors (5xx), timeouts and connection errors are retried with exponential backoff and jitter, waiting as long as the provider's Retry-After header asks when it sends one. After a 429, every call to that model waits too, so they don't all keep hitting the limit. Other errors, such as an invalid API key or a request the model refuses, fail at once.

Errors per note. An error that persists after the retries stops the batch by default. With on_error="record", that note gets an empty result with the error in its error field, and the other notes go on:

extractor = SimpleLLMExtractor(
    model_id="openai/gpt-5-mini",
    entity_definitions=entity_definitions,
    on_error="record",
)
results = await extractor(list_of_notes)
failed = [i for i, r in enumerate(results) if r.error]

SimpleLLMExtractor(max_concurrency=...) still works: it caps the calls of that one extractor, on top of any limit set with set_rate_limits.

docs.title: 3. Entity definitions
docs.text: Entity definitions tell the model what to extract. Each definition has a name, a key, a definition text (this is what the model reads, so write it carefully) and, optionally, a parent and attributes. This section is a summary; see Writing entity definitions for every field, how to choose between them, YAML pitfalls and how to check a file before using it.

docs.title: Predefined definitions
docs.text:
AATM ships definitions aligned with OMOP CDM tables and common clinical scales:

Name Keys condition_occurrence condition_name with required attribute status (confirmed, preliminary); children of a condition: verbatim_start_date, verbatim_end_date drug_exposure drug_name with required attribute kind (administered, prescribed, taking) and attribute route (oral, intravenous, subcutaneous, ...); children of a drug: verbatim_start_date, verbatim_end_date, drug_duration, sig ecog_performance_status ecog_performance_status with attributes score (0-5), or score_range_min / score_range_max for a range such as "ECOG 0-1"; child of a status: assessment_date lab_results lab_test with attribute operator (<, <=, >, >=); children of a test: lab_value, lab_unit, lab_date smoking_status smoking_status with required attribute status (never, former, current_every_day, current_some_day, current_unknown_frequency, not_current); pack_years with child pack_years_value family_history family_history (the condition) with attribute relative (mother, father, sister, ...) medical_history medical_history: a past condition the patient no longer has device_exposure device_name with required attribute kind (placed, existing); children of a device: verbatim_start_date, verbatim_end_date, device_quantity 
EntityDefinitions.from_predefined("drug_exposure")

docs.title: Writing your own
docs.text:
Definitions are a YAML list:

my_definitions.yaml
- name: Allergen
  definition: A substance the patient is allergic to, e.g. "penicillin" or "peanuts".

- name: Reaction
  definition: The reaction caused by an allergen, e.g. "rash" or "anaphylaxis".
  has_parent: true
  parent_key: allergen

entity_definitions = EntityDefinitions.from_yaml("my_definitions.yaml")

Or build them in Python:

from aatm.data_models.extractors import EntityDefinition, EntityDefinitions

entity_definitions = EntityDefinitions(
    entities=[
        EntityDefinition(name="Allergen", definition="A substance the patient is allergic to."),
        EntityDefinition(
            name="Reaction",
            definition="The reaction caused by an allergen.",
            has_parent=True,
            parent_key="allergen",
        ),
    ]
)

Rules:

  • key is optional. If omitted, it is generated from the name: lowercase, accents removed, other characters replaced by _ ("Condição — Início" becomes condicao_inicio). A key you write yourself must already be in that form.
  • Parents: an entity with has_parent: true must set parent_key to the key of another definition, and every extracted mention of it must be linked to a mention of that parent. Hierarchies can have any depth (drug → dose → unit).
  • Invalid files fail when loaded, before any model call, with a message that names the file: keys that are not lowercase snake_case, duplicate keys, a parent_key that does not exist, an entity that is its own parent, has_parent without parent_key (or the reverse), and loops such as a -> b -> a. For example:
ValueError: Invalid entity definitions in my_definitions.yaml:
1 validation error for EntityDefinitions
  Value error, Cycle in entity parent keys: drug_name -> unit -> dose -> drug_name

docs.title: Attributes: classifying each mention
docs.text:
Sometimes you need more than the span: you also want to know what the note says about it. Attributes let the model assign one label from a fixed list to each mention. The label does not have to appear in the text.

brca.yaml
- name: BRCA gene test
  key: brca_test
  definition: A mention of BRCA1 and/or BRCA2 genetic testing performed for the patient.
  attributes:
    - key: result
      description: The result of the test as stated in the note.
      labels:
        - value: positive
          description: A pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant was reported.
        - value: negative
          description: No pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant was found.
        - value: uncertain
          description: Only a variant of uncertain significance (VUS) was reported.
  • Write a description for every label. The model reads them to decide, so they are where you settle edge cases (is a VUS "uncertain" or "negative"?).
  • Attributes are optional by default. When the note does not say, the model leaves the attribute out and the mention is kept without it. It is told never to guess, so "not stated" and a real uncertain result stay distinct.
  • required: true means a mention is only useful with this attribute: a mention without a valid label for it is rejected, with its children (see Attribute issues).

See Attributes for when to use an attribute instead of a child entity, and how to write labels.

docs.title: 4. What the model sees and returns
docs.text:
The note is split into numbered lines before it is sent to the model. Blank lines are skipped and every line keeps its position in the original note:

[L1] ## Problem list
[L2] * Hypertension, diagnosed 2015
[L3] * Type 2 diabetes mellitus and CKD stage 3, both diagnosed 2019
[L4] ## Assessment
[L5] Hypertension worsened since March 2026.

For every mention, the model returns:

Field Meaning id A local id, unique in the response: e1, e2, ... text The exact text, copied from the line key The entity key from the definitions line The line the mention is on, e.g. L2 occurrence Only when the same text appears more than once on that line: which one (1-based) parents The ids of the parent mentions, e.g. ["e1"]; several parents are allowed attributes Labels for the entity's attributes, e.g. [{"key": "result", "value": "negative"}]; attributes the note does not state are left out

Because each mention has a line and each link points to an id, the result is unambiguous: the 2015 above belongs to the Hypertension on line 2, not the one on line 5.

Lines are kept whole by default. For notes with very long paragraphs (or text that lost its line breaks), you can split long lines at sentence boundaries:

extractor = SimpleLLMExtractor(..., max_segment_chars=400)

The sentence splitter is simple and also splits after abbreviations such as p.o., so only enable it when your notes need it.

docs.title: 5. Validation
docs.text:
The model output is never trusted as is. Each candidate is checked, and the ones that fail are kept in result.unmatched_entities with the reasons:

Reason Meaning invalid_line The line id does not exist invalid_text The text does not appear anywhere in the note text_not_in_line The text is in the note, but not on the given line invalid_occurrence The line has fewer copies of the text than occurrence invalid_key The key is not in the entity definitions required_parent_missing The entity needs a parent but lists none invalid_parent A parent id does not exist or has the wrong key parent_rejected A parent was itself rejected unexpected_parent An entity without a parent definition lists parents duplicate_id An id was reused; the first entity keeps it duplicate The same mention (same span and key) was extracted twice required_attribute_missing A required attribute was not given invalid_required_attribute A required attribute was given with a label that is not defined

Matching is exact: case, spacing and punctuation must be identical to the note. Small formatting slips are tolerated: line may be written L4, [L4] or 4, and a copied [L4] prefix is removed from text.

When the same mention is extracted twice, the first one is kept, the parents of both are combined, and any child pointing at the dropped copy is relinked to the kept one.

For the note above, a response with three deliberate mistakes gives:

Validated:
  e1  condition_name       'Hypertension'              L2  [18:30]   parents=[]
  e2  verbatim_start_date  '2015'                      L2  [42:46]   parents=['e1']
  e3  condition_name       'Type 2 diabetes mellitus'  L3  [49:73]   parents=[]
  e4  condition_name       'CKD stage 3'               L3  [78:89]   parents=[]
  e5  verbatim_start_date  '2019'                      L3  [106:110] parents=['e3', 'e4']
  e6  condition_name       'Hypertension'              L5  [126:138] parents=[]
Rejected:
  e7  'March 2026'    L4  ['text_not_in_line']   # the text is on L5
  e8  '2026'          L5  ['invalid_parent']     # its parent id does not exist
  e9  'Hypertension'  L2  ['duplicate']          # same mention as e1

result.unmatched_keys lists the definition keys with no validated entity (here ['verbatim_end_date']), which helps spot what the model never found.

docs.title: Attribute issues
docs.text:
A wrong label never throws away a valid span unless the attribute is required. Every problem is recorded as an AttributeIssue with the candidate id, the entity key, the attribute key, the value the model gave and a reason, so you can see which attribute causes trouble:

Reason Meaning What is kept unknown_attribute The entity has no attribute with this key The span, without it invalid_label The value is not one of the defined labels The span, without it (rejected if the attribute is required) missing_required A required attribute was not given Nothing: the span is rejected conflicting_values The same attribute was given twice with different values The first valid value conflicting_duplicate A duplicate mention gave a different value The first mention's value (kept_entity_id, kept_value)

Issues are split by the attribute's definition:

  • result.required_attribute_issues: issues on required attributes. A missing_required or invalid_label here means the mention was rejected (and its children, with parent_rejected).
  • result.optional_attribute_issues: issues on optional or unknown attributes. The mention was kept.

Three more rules decide what is reported:

  • Case and surrounding spaces are ignored. A model answer of " Negative " is accepted as negative, stored exactly as defined, and not reported. Only values that match no label become invalid_label.
  • Attributes are checked only for candidates that pass every other check. A candidate rejected for its text, line, key or parent adds no attribute issues, so the issue counts cover only mentions that were really found.
  • Duplicates keep the first mention's labels. A label the kept mention lacks is copied from the duplicate, a different label is reported as conflicting_duplicate, and a duplicate that is missing a required attribute is not reported, since the kept mention already has it.

To find the attributes that cause the most problems across many notes:

from collections import Counter

counts = Counter(
    (issue.entity_key, issue.attribute_key, issue.reason)
    for result in results
    for issue in result.required_attribute_issues + result.optional_attribute_issues
)

docs.title: 6. Working with the results
docs.text:
extractor(...) returns one EntityValidationResult per note:

Attribute / method Content validated_entities Validated entities in document order, each with id, key, text, line, start, end, parents (ids) and valid attributes; entity.get_attribute("result") returns one label unmatched_entities Rejected candidates with their reasons unmatched_keys Definition keys with no validated entity required_attribute_issues Problems with required attributes optional_attribute_issues Problems with optional or unknown attributes get_entity(id) One validated entity by id to_records() Entities nested under their parents

docs.title: Follow links between entities
docs.text:
date = result.get_entity("e5")
[result.get_entity(p).text for p in date.parents]
# ['Type 2 diabetes mellitus', 'CKD stage 3']

start and end are character offsets in the original note, so note[entity.start:entity.end] == entity.text always holds.

docs.title: Records view
docs.text:
to_records() returns one record per entity without parents, with its children grouped by key. A child with several parents appears under each of them:

for record in result.to_records():
    print(record.text, record.line, {k: [c.text for c in v] for k, v in record.children.items()})

Hypertension L2 {'verbatim_start_date': ['2015']}
Type 2 diabetes mellitus L3 {'verbatim_start_date': ['2019']}
CKD stage 3 L3 {'verbatim_start_date': ['2019']}
Hypertension L5 {}

Each record also has attributes, a plain {key: label} dict, e.g. {"result": "negative"}.

docs.title: Building table rows
docs.text:
Records map naturally to OMOP-like rows:

rows = []
for record in result.to_records():
    starts = record.children.get("verbatim_start_date", [])
    ends = record.children.get("verbatim_end_date", [])
    rows.append(
        {
            "condition_source_value": record.text,
            "verbatim_start_date": starts[0].text if starts else None,
            "verbatim_end_date": ends[0].text if ends else None,
            "evidence": f"{record.line} [{record.start}:{record.end}]",
        }
    )

Dates are returned exactly as written in the note ("2015", "March 2026") and still need to be normalized, and condition_source_value still needs to be mapped to a standard concept.

docs.title: 7. Validating without calling a model
docs.text:
validate_extracted_entity works on any model output that follows the ExtractedEntityCandidates schema. This is useful in tests, or to validate the output of a model called outside AATM:

from aatm.data_models.extractors import (
    ExtractedEntityCandidates,
    validate_extracted_entity,
)

candidates = ExtractedEntityCandidates.model_validate(
    {
        "entities": [
            {"id": "e1", "text": "Hypertension", "key": "condition_name", "line": "L2", "occurrence": None, "parents": []},
            {"id": "e2", "text": "2015", "key": "verbatim_start_date", "line": "L2", "occurrence": None, "parents": ["e1"]},
        ]
    }
)
result = validate_extracted_entity(note, entity_definitions, candidates)

The line ids are computed with segment_text(note). If you used max_segment_chars, pass the same segments: validate_extracted_entity(note, defs, candidates, segments=segment_text(note, max_segment_chars=400)).

docs.title: 8. Customizing the extractor
docs.text:
Argument Default Purpose model_id required unless llm is given <provider>/<model>, see Requirements entity_definitions required What to extract api_key None Provider key; the provider's environment variable is used when omitted base_url None Server URL for OpenAI-compatible providers settings None aatm.llm.LLMSettings or a dict, e.g. {"temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 8000} llm None A ready-made aatm.llm.StructuredLLM, used instead of model_id max_concurrency None Parallel model calls from this extractor; None means no cap of its own (see Rate limits and retries) on_error "raise" "record" returns an empty result with the error for a note that fails after retries max_segment_chars None Split lines longer than this at sentence boundaries instructions built-in prompt Custom system prompt; {output_format} and {entity_definitions} are filled in

settings accepts temperature, max_tokens, reasoning_effort ("minimal" to "max"), timeout (seconds) and provider_kwargs (extra arguments passed as-is to the provider's API call). Settings left unset use the provider's defaults. Current Anthropic models do not accept temperature, so it is ignored there with a warning.

When writing custom instructions, keep the explanation of line ids, ids, parents and attributes from the built-in prompt (aatm.extractors.llm_extractors.DEFAULT_INSTRUCTION); validation expects them.

docs.title: 9. Debugging
docs.text:
AATM is silent by default. To see what validation does:

import logging
import aatm

aatm.configure_logging()  # shows AATM messages on stderr
logging.getLogger("aatm.data_models.extractors").setLevel(logging.DEBUG)

The unmatched_entities reasons are usually the fastest way to understand a poor extraction: many text_not_in_line rejections point to line-id mistakes, and many invalid_text rejections to paraphrased spans.

docs.title: 10. Current limitations
docs.text:
• Matching is exact; spans with different case or spacing than the note are rejected.
  • The predefined definitions say in their own words what to leave out: condition_occurrence excludes negated, ruled-out and past conditions and those of relatives; drug_exposure excludes negated, considered-only and allergy mentions. For other cases you can add your own attributes, e.g. an assertion attribute with present, absent and possible.
  • Attribute labels come from a single extraction call; there is no separate classification pass per mention yet.
  • GeminiExtractor (also in aatm.extractors) is an older interface based on ExtractionTask and does not use entity definitions or this validation.

docs.title: Python API Quick Start
docs.text: This page shows how to use AATM from the Python API.

docs.title: What you can do from the Python API
docs.text:
With the Python API, you can:

  • initialize and configure a terminology mapping pipeline in code
  • load translators, retrievers, rerankers, and selectors from registries
  • instantiate TerminologyMapper directly
  • build a mapper from a structured task configuration
  • run mapping jobs from Python
  • work with pipeline components individually
  • compose stages with the | operator

The package exposes dedicated base classes and concrete implementations for translators, retrievers, rerankers, selectors, and the main TerminologyMapper orchestration class.

docs.title: 1. Understand the main Python entry point
docs.text:
The main class is TerminologyMapper.

It orchestrates the full mapping workflow by combining:

  • a translator
  • a retriever
  • an optional reranker
  • a selector

Its constructor accepts these components directly, along with settings such as input_file, output_dir, batch_size, rate_limit, column_mapping, and limit_to. It also provides defaults when some components are omitted.

Conceptually, the pipeline looks like this:

flowchart LR
    A[Source Concepts] --> B[Translator]
    B --> C[Retriever]
    C --> D[Reranker]
    D --> E[Selector]
    E --> F[Mapped Results]

The mapping flow inside TerminologyMapper.map() processes source concepts in batches, translates them, retrieves candidates, optionally reranks them, selects final matches, and writes the output DataFrame to disk.

docs.title: 2. Example
docs.text:
A good first setup is:

  • empty-translator
  • embeddinggemma-300M
  • bm25-reranker
  • first-result-selector

These can be loaded from the package registries and passed into TerminologyMapper. 

from aatm.terminology_mapper import TerminologyMapper
from aatm.registries.translators import load_translator
from aatm.registries.retrievers import load_retriever
from aatm.registries.rerankers import load_reranker
from aatm.registries.selectors import load_selector

mapper = TerminologyMapper(
    translator=load_translator("empty-translator"),
    retriever=load_retriever("embeddinggemma-300M"),
    reranker=load_reranker("bm25-reranker"),
    selector=load_selector("first-result-selector"),
    batch_size=100,
)

results_df = mapper.map("data/source_to_concept_map.csv")
print(results_df.head())

docs.title: 3. Prepare your input CSV
docs.text:
The mapper expects an OMOP-style SOURCE_TO_CONCEPT_MAP input structure.

The required columns checked by map_csv_to_source_concepts() are:

  • source_code
  • source_concept_id
  • source_vocabulary_id
  • source_code_description
  • valid_start_date
  • valid_end_date
  • invalid_reason

These required columns are hardcoded in TerminologyMapper.expected_columns, and the CSV loader validates them before continuing.

Example:

source_code,source_concept_id,source_vocabulary_id,source_code_description,valid_start_date,valid_end_date,invalid_reason
A01,,LOCAL,"Dor no peito",2020-01-01,2099-12-31,
B02,,LOCAL,"Diabetes mellitus tipo 2",2020-01-01,2099-12-31,

docs.title: 4. Run mapping from Python
docs.text:
Once your mapper is configured, run mapping like this:

results_df = mapper.map("data/source_to_concept_map.csv")

You can also limit the number of rows processed during testing:

results_df = mapper.map("data/source_to_concept_map.csv", limit_to=20)

You can control whether confidence scores are included:

results_df = mapper.map(
    "data/source_to_concept_map.csv",
    return_confidence_scores=True,
)

Although source_code_description values are translated as defined by the translator, the original values are stored in the column source_code_description_original.

The map() method writes the mapped results to mapped_source_concepts.csv inside the configured output directory and returns the resulting DataFrame.

docs.title: 5. Use custom column names
docs.text:
If your CSV uses different column names, pass column_mapping when constructing the mapper.

map_csv_to_source_concepts() renames columns using this mapping before validating the expected schema.

Note that the TerminologyMapper class won't create the required columns for you. You need to prepare the table beforehand.

from aatm.terminology_mapper import TerminologyMapper
from aatm.registries.translators import load_translator
from aatm.registries.retrievers import load_retriever
from aatm.registries.rerankers import load_reranker
from aatm.registries.selectors import load_selector

mapper = TerminologyMapper(
    translator=load_translator("empty-translator"),
    retriever=load_retriever("embeddinggemma-300M"),
    reranker=load_reranker("bm25-reranker"),
    selector=load_selector("first-result-selector"),
    column_mapping={
        "code": "source_code",
        "description": "source_code_description",
        "vocabulary": "source_vocabulary_id",
        "start_date": "valid_start_date",
        "end_date": "valid_end_date",
        "reason": "invalid_reason",
        "concept_id": "source_concept_id",
    },
)

results_df = mapper.map("data/my_input.csv")

docs.title: 6. Build a mapper from a task configuration object
docs.text:
You can also create the mapper from a structured TerminologyMappingTask object by calling TerminologyMapper.from_task_config().

That classmethod resolves the configured translator, retriever, selector, and reranker from their registries and returns a ready-to-use mapper.

from pathlib import Path

from aatm.data_models import TerminologyMappingTask
from aatm.terminology_mapper import TerminologyMapper

task = TerminologyMappingTask(
    input_file=Path("data/source_to_concept_map.csv"),
    output_dir=Path("output"),
    translator_id="empty-translator",
    retriever_id="embeddinggemma-300M",
    reranker_id="bm25-reranker",
    selector_id="first-result-selector",
    batch_size=100,
    rate_limit=None,
    limit_to=None,
)

mapper = TerminologyMapper.from_task_config(task)
results_df = mapper.map()

docs.title: 7. Load components directly from registries
docs.text: The package provides registry loaders for translators, retrievers, rerankers, and selectors.

docs.title: Translators
docs.text:
The translator registry exposes at least:

  • empty-translator
  • gemini-2.5-flash

through load_translator(name, **kwargs). 

from aatm.registries.translators import load_translator

translator = load_translator("empty-translator")

docs.title: Retrievers
docs.text:
Retriever models are loaded with load_retriever(model_name), which constructs a ChromaDBRetriever backed by the configured embedding function and ChromaDB path, or a PineconeRetriever when AATM_VECTOR_DB=pinecone (see Environment variables).

Common registered retriever IDs include:

  • qwen3-06B
  • qwen3-4B
  • gemini-embedding-001
  • embeddinggemma-300M
  • text-embedding-3-small
  • text-embedding-3-large 
from aatm.registries.retrievers import load_retriever

retriever = load_retriever("embeddinggemma-300M")

docs.title: Rerankers
docs.text:
The reranker registry exposes:

  • bm25-reranker
  • qwen3-reranker-0.6b
  • qwen3-reranker-4b
  • qwen3-reranker-8b 
from aatm.registries.rerankers import load_reranker

reranker = load_reranker("bm25-reranker")

docs.title: Selectors
docs.text:
The selector registry exposes:

  • first-result-selector
  • gpt-5.2
  • gpt-5
  • gpt-5-mini
  • gpt-5-nano
  • gemini-3-pro-preview
  • gemini-3-flash-preview
  • gemini-2.5-flash
  • gemini-2.5-flash-lite
  • gemini-2.5-pro
  • agent-gpt-5-mini, agent-gpt-5, agent-gpt-5.2, agent-gemini-3-flash-preview, agent-gemini-2.5-flash: the concept search agent (see below)
from aatm.registries.selectors import load_selector

selector = load_selector("first-result-selector")

docs.title: Agentic selector
docs.text:
The other selectors can only pick among the retrieved candidates. AgenticSelector starts from them, and when none fits, an LLM agent searches further: its own semantic searches with the mapper's retriever (expanding abbreviations, translating), lexical search over concept names and synonyms, code lookups, concept details and the hierarchy, in the vocabulary database built by aatm init. Each source concept's code and vocabulary are given to the agent, so ICD10CM E11 can be looked up directly.

from aatm.concept_search import AgenticSelector
from aatm.terminology_mapper import TerminologyMapper

mapper = TerminologyMapper(
    input_file="source_concepts.csv",
    retriever="text-embedding-3-small",
    selector=AgenticSelector("openai/gpt-5-mini", max_tool_calls=8),
)
df = mapper.map()
df[["source_code_description", "target_concept_id", "confidence_score", "mapping_rationale"]]

The output gains a mapping_rationale column (the agent's reason) and a mapping_trace column (its searches, as JSON). confidence_score is the agent's confidence level: 0.9 (high), 0.6 (medium) or 0.3 (low); see Searching with an agent. Any aatm.llm model id works, e.g. "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5" or "ollama/llama3.3". The same agent codes extracted text in OMOP tables, with aatm.omop.AgenticCoder.

docs.title: 8. Work with components directly in Python
docs.text: You do not need to go through TerminologyMapper for every workflow. The components are callable and can be used independently.

docs.title: Translator example
docs.text:
BaseTranslator.__call__() accepts a string, a list of strings, or a list of SourceConcept objects and returns a list of Translation objects. 

from aatm.registries.translators import load_translator

translator = load_translator("empty-translator")
translations = translator(["Dor no peito", "Tosse"])
print(translations)

docs.title: Retriever example
docs.text:
BaseRetriever.__call__() accepts a string, a Translation, a list of strings, or a list of Translation objects and returns RetrieverResults. 

from aatm.registries.retrievers import load_retriever

retriever = load_retriever("embeddinggemma-300M")
results = retriever(["chest pain", "cough"])
print(results)

docs.title: Reranker example
docs.text:
Rerankers consume RetrieverResults and return reordered RetrieverResults. 

from aatm.registries.rerankers import load_reranker

reranker = load_reranker("bm25-reranker")
reranked = reranker(results)
print(reranked)

docs.title: Selector example
docs.text:
Selectors consume RetrieverResults and return SelectorResults. 

from aatm.registries.selectors import load_selector

selector = load_selector("first-result-selector")
selected = selector(reranked)
print(selected)

docs.title: 9. Compose the pipeline with |
docs.text:
AATM components inherit pipeline behavior from PipelineBaseClass, which overloads the | operator.

That means you can compose stages directly in Python:

from aatm.registries.translators import load_translator
from aatm.registries.retrievers import load_retriever
from aatm.registries.rerankers import load_reranker
from aatm.registries.selectors import load_selector

translator = load_translator("empty-translator")
retriever = load_retriever("embeddinggemma-300M")
reranker = load_reranker("bm25-reranker")
selector = load_selector("first-result-selector")

selected = (
    ["Dor no peito", "Tosse"]
    | translator
    | retriever
    | reranker
    | selector
)

print(selected)

Inside TerminologyMapper.map(), the same style is used for the core pipeline flow.

docs.title: 10. Understand the default behaviors
docs.text:
If you instantiate TerminologyMapper() without passing components:

  • translator defaults to EmptyTranslator()
  • retriever defaults to a ChromaDBRetriever backed by GoogleEmbeddingFunction(model="gemini-embedding-001")
  • selector defaults to FirstResultSelector()
  • reranker defaults to PipelineBaseClass() as an identity-like empty reranker stage

That can be convenient, but for reproducible setups it is usually better to pass your components explicitly.

docs.title: 11. Asynchronous mapping
docs.text:
TerminologyMapper also defines an amap() method for asynchronous mapping. It follows the same high-level idea as map(), processing source concepts in batches and returning a DataFrame.

A minimal pattern looks like this:

import asyncio

from aatm.terminology_mapper import TerminologyMapper

mapper = TerminologyMapper()

async def main():
    df = await mapper.amap("data/source_to_concept_map.csv", limit_to=20)
    print(df.head())

asyncio.run(main())

Use this only if your configured components support the async flow you want.

docs.title: 12. What gets created locally
docs.text:
A normal Python workflow may create or use local artifacts such as:

.aatm/
├── omop.db
├── datasets/
└── chroma_vector_dbs/

Mapped outputs are typically written to:

output/mapped_source_concepts.csv

The retriever registry also derives ChromaDB paths from .aatm/chroma_vector_dbs/<model_name>.

docs.title: End-to-end Python example
docs.text:
Here is a full Python-only path.

from aatm.terminology_mapper import TerminologyMapper
from aatm.registries.translators import load_translator
from aatm.registries.retrievers import load_retriever
from aatm.registries.rerankers import load_reranker
from aatm.registries.selectors import load_selector

mapper = TerminologyMapper(
    translator=load_translator("empty-translator"),
    retriever=load_retriever("embeddinggemma-300M"),
    reranker=load_reranker("bm25-reranker"),
    selector=load_selector("first-result-selector"),
    batch_size=100,
    output_dir="output",
)

results_df = mapper.map(
    file_path="data/source_to_concept_map.csv",
    limit_to=50,
    return_confidence_scores=True,
)

print(results_df.head())

docs.title: The retriever fails because the local vector database is missing
docs.text: Make sure you already created the local ChromaDB resources for the retriever model you want to use.

docs.title: Your CSV fails validation
docs.text: Make sure your input file contains the expected OMOP columns, or pass column_mapping.

docs.title: API-backed components fail
docs.text: Check your .env file and confirm the required API keys are present.

docs.title: A selector or reranker name is rejected
docs.text: Use one of the registered names shown in this page. The registry loaders raise ValueError when a name is unknown.

docs.title: Command Line Interface
docs.text:
This module defines the main Typer application for the Any-to-Any Terminology Mapping (AATM) package. It provides commands for initializing the local project environment, launching the search user interface, and running terminology mapping tasks from either a config file or command-line options.

The CLI is responsible for orchestrating high-level workflows such as:

  • setting up local helper directories and Git ignore rules
  • validating vocabulary and embedding model inputs
  • building local SQLite and vector databases for terminology mapping
  • collecting interactive user input for setup choices
  • loading and displaying mapping task configurations
  • starting synchronous terminology mapping runs
  • launching the Streamlit-based search interface

Commands:

  • init: Set up the local environment for OMOP vocabulary processing and vector database creation.

  • search-ui: Launch the Streamlit-based search interface.

  • map: Run a terminology mapping task from a configuration file or from explicit CLI arguments.

  • amap: Placeholder for future asynchronous mapping support.

  • serve: Serves a minimal FastAPI application with AATM's functionality.

  • doctor: Check whether local models can use a GPU and print the commands that enable it.

Attributes:

Name Type Description LOCAL_HELPER_PATH Path

Path to the local helper directory used by AATM to store generated artifacts and local resources.

DEFAULT_VOCAB_DIR Path

Default directory containing OMOP vocabulary files.

DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_MODEL str

Default embedding model used when building the local vector database.

SUPPORTED_EMBEDDING_MODELS List[str]

List of embedding model identifiers supported by the CLI setup workflow.

STANDARD_VOCABULARIES List[str]

List of supported standard vocabularies available for terminology mapping.

DEFAULT_STANDARD_VOCABULARIES List[str]

Default subset of standard vocabularies selected during initialization.

AATM_LOGO str

Multiline ASCII logo displayed in the CLI welcome screen.

Examples:

Initialize the local environment with defaults:

$ aatm init

Initialize with a custom vocabulary directory:

$ aatm init --vocab-dir ./vocabularies

Run a mapping task from a config file:

$ aatm map --task-config-path config.yaml

Run a mapping task from explicit options:

$ aatm map --input-file concepts.csv --output-dir outputs \
    --translator-id my_translator --retriever-id my_retriever \
    --selector-id my_selector

Launch the search UI:

$ aatm search-ui

Check GPU support:

$ aatm doctor
Note

This module is intended to serve as the main CLI entrypoint for the package. It coordinates user interaction and delegates implementation details to lower-level utilities and domain-specific components.

docs.title: ensure_utf8_output()
docs.text:
Make the CLI's output streams UTF-8 so non-ASCII output cannot crash it.

On Windows, Python uses the legacy code page (e.g. cp1252) when stdout/stderr are redirected to a file or pipe, and printing the logo or other non-ASCII text then raises UnicodeEncodeError. Interactive consoles already use UTF-8 and are left as they are. PYTHONIOENCODING is set so that subprocesses started by the CLI (serve, search-ui) behave the same, unless the user already set it.

Source code in aatm/main.py 
def ensure_utf8_output() -> None:
    """Make the CLI's output streams UTF-8 so non-ASCII output cannot crash it.

    On Windows, Python uses the legacy code page (e.g. cp1252) when stdout/stderr are
    redirected to a file or pipe, and printing the logo or other non-ASCII text then
    raises `UnicodeEncodeError`. Interactive consoles already use UTF-8 and are left
    as they are. `PYTHONIOENCODING` is set so that subprocesses started by the CLI
    (`serve`, `search-ui`) behave the same, unless the user already set it.
    """
    for stream in (sys.stdout, sys.stderr):
        encoding = (getattr(stream, "encoding", None) or "").replace("-", "").lower()
        reconfigure = getattr(stream, "reconfigure", None)
        if encoding != "utf8" and reconfigure is not None:
            try:
                reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
            except (ValueError, OSError):
                # Not reconfigurable (e.g. already written to in a way that
                # prevents it); keep the original stream.
                pass

    os.environ.setdefault("PYTHONIOENCODING", "utf-8")

def prepare_vocab_bundle(
    source: str,
    vocab_dir: Path,
    *,
    force: bool = False,
    umls_api_key: Optional[str] = None,
    standard_vocabs: Optional[List[str]] = None,
) -> Path:
    """Download (if needed), unpack and check an Athena vocabulary bundle.

    Args:
        source: The bundle's download link, or the path of the zip.
        vocab_dir: Directory to unpack the bundle into.
        force: Overwrite existing files in `vocab_dir` without asking.
        umls_api_key: UMLS API key for the CPT4 step; skipped when missing.
        standard_vocabs: Standard vocabularies the user asked for, to warn
            when the bundle does not include them.

    Returns:
        The directory holding the vocabulary CSVs.

    Raises:
        typer.Exit: With a message when any step fails.
    """
    from rich.progress import (
        BarColumn,
        DownloadColumn,
        Progress,
        TimeRemainingColumn,
        TransferSpeedColumn,
    )

    from aatm import vocab_bundle as vb

    console.print("[blue]0) Preparing the Athena vocabulary bundle[/blue]")
    try:
        if vb.is_url(source):
            console.print("Downloading the bundle...")
            with Progress(
                "[progress.description]{task.description}",
                BarColumn(),
                DownloadColumn(),
                TransferSpeedColumn(),
                TimeRemainingColumn(),
                console=console,
                transient=True,
            ) as bar:
                task = bar.add_task("Downloading", total=None)
                zip_path = vb.download_bundle(
                    source,
                    LOCAL_HELPER_PATH / "downloads",
                    progress=lambda done, total: bar.update(
                        task, completed=done, total=total
                    ),
                )
            console.print(f"Saved the bundle to '{zip_path}'.")
        else:
            zip_path = Path(source).expanduser()

        console.print(f"Unpacking '{zip_path}' into '{vocab_dir}'...")
        try:
            vb.unpack_bundle(zip_path, vocab_dir, overwrite=force)
        except vb.VocabFilesExistError as e:
            if not sys.stdin.isatty():
                console.print(
                    f"[yellow]OOPS![/yellow] {e}. Pass --force to overwrite them, "
                    "or choose another directory with --vocab-dir.\n"
                )
                raise typer.Exit(1)
            if not questionary.confirm(f"{e}. Overwrite them?", default=False).ask():
                console.print(
                    "Nothing was overwritten. Choose another directory with "
                    "--vocab-dir, or pass --force.\n"
                )
                raise typer.Exit(1)
            vb.unpack_bundle(zip_path, vocab_dir, overwrite=True)
    except vb.VocabBundleError as e:
        console.print(f"[yellow]OOPS![/yellow] {e}\n")
        raise typer.Exit(1)

    missing = vb.missing_required_files(vocab_dir)
    if missing:
        console.print(
            f"[yellow]OOPS![/yellow] The bundle is missing required files: "
            f"{', '.join(missing)}. Request a new bundle at {vb.ATHENA_URL}.\n"
        )
        raise typer.Exit(1)

    if vb.has_cpt4_tooling(vocab_dir):
        if not umls_api_key:
            console.print(
                "[yellow]Warning:[/yellow] the bundle includes CPT4, but no UMLS "
                "API key was given, so CPT4 concepts will have no names. Pass "
                f"--umls-api-key or set {vb.UMLS_API_KEY_ENV_VAR} to add them "
                "(get a key at https://uts.nlm.nih.gov/uts/profile)."
            )
        else:
            console.print("Adding CPT4 concept names (this can take a while)...")
            try:
                vb.run_cpt4(vocab_dir, umls_api_key)
            except vb.Cpt4Error as e:
                console.print(f"[yellow]OOPS![/yellow] {e}\n")
                raise typer.Exit(1)

    vocabularies = vb.read_bundle_vocabularies(vocab_dir)
    listed = sorted(
        (v for v in vocabularies if not v.omop_generated),
        key=lambda v: v.vocabulary_id.lower(),
    )
    if listed:
        console.print(f"The bundle contains {len(listed)} vocabularies:")
        for v in listed:
            console.print(f"  - {v.vocabulary_id}: {v.version or 'no version'}")
    internal = len(vocabularies) - len(listed)
    if internal:
        console.print(
            f"  and {internal} vocabularies generated by OMOP (Visit, Gender, ...)."
        )
    present = {v.vocabulary_id for v in vocabularies}
    for vocab in standard_vocabs or []:
        if vocab not in present:
            console.print(
                f"[yellow]Warning:[/yellow] {vocab} was requested with "
                "--standard-vocabs but is not in the bundle."
            )
    console.print("[green]Done![/green]\n")
    return vocab_dir

docs.text:
Initialize the local AATM environment.

This command prepares the local project environment required for terminology mapping with OMOP vocabularies. It creates the helper directory used by AATM, ensures .aatm is listed in .gitignore, validates user inputs, builds the local SQLite vocabulary database, prepares mapping datasets for the selected standard vocabularies, and creates the local vector database used for retrieval.

When embedding_model or standard_vocabs are not provided, the command interactively prompts the user to choose among the supported options.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default vocab_dir Annotated[Optional[Path], Option(--vocab - dir, -vd, help='Path to the OMOP vocabularies directory.', show_default=False)]

Name of the embedding model to use for building the local vector database. If not provided, the user is prompted to select one interactively.

Defaults to the precision of the model's checkpoint. Half precision is faster and uses less GPU memory, but requires an NVIDIA GPU. Overrides AATM_EMBEDDING_DTYPE.", show_default=False)]

Precision for local embedding models. If not provided, AATM_EMBEDDING_DTYPE is used, and otherwise the precision of the model's checkpoint.

List of standard vocabularies to include in the mapping datasets. If not provided, the user is prompted to select one or more interactively.

Overrides AATM_VECTOR_DB. Defaults to 'local'.", show_default=False)]

Where to build the vector database, local, cloud or pinecone. If not provided, AATM_VECTOR_DB is used, and otherwise local.

None vocab_zip Annotated[Optional[str], Option(--vocab - zip, help='Athena vocabulary bundle to set up from: the download link Athena emailed, or the path of the downloaded zip. It is unpacked into --vocab-dir (default ./vocabularies).', show_default=False)]

An Athena vocabulary bundle, as its download link or the path of the zip. It is downloaded if needed, unpacked into vocab_dir, and its CPT4 names are added when it includes CPT4.

$ aatm init

Initialize with a custom vocabulary directory:

Set up from the bundle link Athena emailed, or from the downloaded zip:

$ aatm init --vocab-zip "https://athena.ohdsi.org/api/v1/vocabularies/zip/<id>"
$ aatm init --vocab-zip ~/Downloads/vocabulary_download_v5_<id>.zip

Initialize with an explicit embedding model:

$ aatm init --embedding-model qwen3-4B

Build the vector database in half precision on an NVIDIA GPU:
