@app.command(
    help="Set up your environment to work with OMOP vocabularies and create terminology mappings."
)
def init(
    vocab_dir: Annotated[
        Optional[Path],
        typer.Option(
            "--vocab-dir",
            "-vd",
            help="Path to the OMOP vocabularies directory.",
            show_default=False,
        ),
    ] = None,
    embedding_model: Annotated[
        Optional[str],
        typer.Option(
            "--embedding-model",
            "-e",
            help="Name of the embedding model to use.",
            show_default=False,
        ),
    ] = None,
    embedding_dtype: Annotated[
        Optional[str],
        typer.Option(
            "--embedding-dtype",
            help=(
                "Precision for local embedding models: float32, bfloat16 or "
                "float16. Defaults to the precision of the model's checkpoint. "
                "Half precision is faster and uses less GPU memory, but requires "
                "an NVIDIA GPU. Overrides AATM_EMBEDDING_DTYPE."
            ),
            show_default=False,
        ),
    ] = None,
    standard_vocabs: Annotated[
        Optional[List[str]],
        typer.Option(
            "--standard-vocabs",
            "-sv",
            help=f"List of standard vocabularies to use. Available options: {STANDARD_VOCABULARIES}.",
        ),
    ] = None,
    vector_db: Annotated[
        Optional[str],
        typer.Option(
            "--vector-db",
            help=(
                "Where to build the vector database: 'local' (ChromaDB on this "
                "machine), 'cloud' (Chroma Cloud, configured with CHROMA_API_KEY) "
                "or 'pinecone' (configured with PINECONE_API_KEY). "
                "Overrides AATM_VECTOR_DB. Defaults to 'local'."
            ),
            show_default=False,
        ),
    ] = None,
    vocab_zip: Annotated[
        Optional[str],
        typer.Option(
            "--vocab-zip",
            help=(
                "Athena vocabulary bundle to set up from: the download link "
                "Athena emailed, or the path of the downloaded zip. It is "
                "unpacked into --vocab-dir (default ./vocabularies)."
            ),
            show_default=False,
        ),
    ] = None,
    force: Annotated[
        bool,
        typer.Option(
            "--force",
            help="With --vocab-zip, overwrite existing vocabulary files without asking.",
        ),
    ] = False,
    umls_api_key: Annotated[
        Optional[str],
        typer.Option(
            "--umls-api-key",
            envvar="UMLS_API_KEY",
            help=(
                "UMLS API key used to add the CPT4 names when the bundle "
                "includes CPT4. Read from UMLS_API_KEY when not given."
            ),
            show_default=False,
            show_envvar=True,
        ),
    ] = None,
) -> None:
    """Initialize the local AATM environment.

    This command prepares the local project environment required for
    terminology mapping with OMOP vocabularies. It creates the helper
    directory used by AATM, ensures `.aatm` is listed in `.gitignore`,
    validates user inputs, builds the local SQLite vocabulary database,
    prepares mapping datasets for the selected standard vocabularies,
    and creates the local vector database used for retrieval.

    When `embedding_model` or `standard_vocabs` are not provided, the
    command interactively prompts the user to choose among the supported
    options.

    Args:
        vocab_dir: Path to the directory containing the OMOP vocabulary
            files. If not provided, the default vocabulary directory is
            used.
        embedding_model: Name of the embedding model to use for building
            the local vector database. If not provided, the user is
            prompted to select one interactively.
        embedding_dtype: Precision for local embedding models. If not
            provided, `AATM_EMBEDDING_DTYPE` is used, and otherwise the
            precision of the model's checkpoint.
        standard_vocabs: List of standard vocabularies to include in the
            mapping datasets. If not provided, the user is prompted to
            select one or more interactively.
        vector_db: Where to build the vector database, ``local``,
            ``cloud`` or ``pinecone``. If not provided, `AATM_VECTOR_DB` is
            used, and otherwise ``local``.
        vocab_zip: An Athena vocabulary bundle, as its download link or the
            path of the zip. It is downloaded if needed, unpacked into
            `vocab_dir`, and its CPT4 names are added when it includes CPT4.
        force: Overwrite existing vocabulary files when unpacking
            `vocab_zip` without asking.
        umls_api_key: UMLS API key for the CPT4 step. If not provided,
            `UMLS_API_KEY` is used; without a key the CPT4 step is skipped.

    Raises:
        typer.Exit: If the vocabulary directory does not exist, if the
            embedding model is not supported, if any provided
            standard vocabulary is invalid, or if the vector database
            configuration is invalid.

    Examples:
        Initialize using the default vocabulary directory:

            $ aatm init

        Initialize with a custom vocabulary directory:

            $ aatm init --vocab-dir ./vocabularies

        Set up from the bundle link Athena emailed, or from the downloaded zip:

            $ aatm init --vocab-zip "https://athena.ohdsi.org/api/v1/vocabularies/zip/<id>"
            $ aatm init --vocab-zip ~/Downloads/vocabulary_download_v5_<id>.zip

        Initialize with an explicit embedding model:

            $ aatm init --embedding-model qwen3-4B

        Build the vector database in half precision on an NVIDIA GPU:

            $ aatm init --embedding-model qwen3-4B --embedding-dtype bfloat16

        Initialize with specific standard vocabularies:

            $ aatm init --standard-vocabs LOINC --standard-vocabs SNOMED

        Build the vector database in Chroma Cloud (needs CHROMA_API_KEY):

            $ aatm init --vector-db cloud

        Build the vector database in Pinecone (needs PINECONE_API_KEY and
        the `aatm[pinecone]` extra):

            $ aatm init --vector-db pinecone
    """
    # Setup local directories
    LOCAL_HELPER_PATH.mkdir(exist_ok=True, parents=True)
    gitignore_path = Path(".gitignore")
    entry = ".aatm"
    if not gitignore_path.exists():
        gitignore_path.write_text(entry + "\n")
    else:
        lines = {line.strip() for line in gitignore_path.read_text().splitlines()}

        if entry not in lines:
            with gitignore_path.open("a") as f:
                f.write(
                    "\n" + entry
                    if not gitignore_path.read_text().endswith("\n")
                    else entry + "\n"
                )

    print_logo()
    console.print("Let's set up your environment!\n")

    # Validate provided standard vocabs
    if standard_vocabs is not None:
        if not set(standard_vocabs).issubset(STANDARD_VOCABULARIES):
            console.print(
                f"[yellow]OOPS![/yellow] You specified standard vocabularies that are not available. Available options: {STANDARD_VOCABULARIES}. You provided: {standard_vocabs}\n"
            )
            raise typer.Exit()

    # Validate vocab directory
    if vocab_zip is not None:
        vocab_dir = prepare_vocab_bundle(
            vocab_zip,
            Path(vocab_dir) if vocab_dir is not None else DEFAULT_VOCAB_DIR,
            force=force,
            umls_api_key=umls_api_key,
            standard_vocabs=standard_vocabs,
        )
    elif vocab_dir is None:
        vocab_dir = DEFAULT_VOCAB_DIR
    else:
        vocab_dir = Path(vocab_dir)
        if not vocab_dir.exists():
            console.print(
                f"[yellow]OOPS![/yellow] You specified a non-existent directory: `{vocab_dir}`. Please, check the path and try again or download the desired OMOP vocabularies at https://athena.ohdsi.org/ if you haven't yet.\n"
            )
            raise typer.Exit()

    if not vocab_dir.exists():
        console.print(
            "[yellow]OOPS![/yellow] You still don't have a `vocabularies` directory. Download the desired OMOP vocabularies at https://athena.ohdsi.org/ and place them in the `./vocabularies` directory or use the `--vocab-dir` option to specify a different directory.\n"
        )
        raise typer.Exit()

    # Validate embedding model
    if embedding_model is not None:
        if embedding_model not in SUPPORTED_EMBEDDING_MODELS:
            console.print(
                f"[yellow]OOPS![/yellow] You specified an unsupported embedding model: `{embedding_model}`. Please, check the model name and try again.\nThe supported embedding models are: {SUPPORTED_EMBEDDING_MODELS}\n"
            )
            raise typer.Exit()

    # Validate the vector database settings before the long build steps.
    from aatm.vector_db import (
        VectorDatabaseConfigError,
        connection_from_env,
        import_pinecone,
    )

    try:
        vector_db_connection = connection_from_env(
            local_path=".aatm/chroma_vector_dbs", mode=vector_db
        )
        if vector_db_connection.mode == "pinecone":
            import_pinecone()
    except VectorDatabaseConfigError as e:
        console.print(f"[yellow]OOPS![/yellow] {e}\n")
        raise typer.Exit()
    vector_db = vector_db_connection.mode

    console.print("[blue]1) Building local OMOP vocabulary database[/blue]")
    console.print(f"Using vocabulary files from: '{vocab_dir}'")

    # Lazy import
    console.print("Preparing local database builder...")

    from aatm.local_database_utils import build_local_sqlite_vocab_database

    build_local_sqlite_vocab_database(vocab_dir)
    console.print("[green]Done![/green]\n")

    console.print(
        "[blue]2) Building vector database[/blue]"
        + {"cloud": " in Chroma Cloud", "pinecone": " in Pinecone"}.get(vector_db, "")
    )

    if embedding_model is None:
        supported_embedding_models_choices = [
            Choice(f"{model_name} (default)", value=model_name)
            if model_name == DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_MODEL
            else Choice(model_name, value=model_name)
            for model_name in SUPPORTED_EMBEDDING_MODELS
        ]
        selected_embedding_model = questionary.select(
            "Select one of the supported embedding models for building the vector database:",
            choices=supported_embedding_models_choices,
            default=DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_MODEL,
        ).ask()
    else:
        console.print(f"Using embedding model: {embedding_model}")
        selected_embedding_model = embedding_model

    if standard_vocabs is None:
        selected_standard_vocabularies = questionary.checkbox(
            "Select one or more standard vocabularies to use for mapping:",
            choices=[
                Choice(
                    vocab, value=vocab, checked=vocab in DEFAULT_STANDARD_VOCABULARIES
                )
                for vocab in STANDARD_VOCABULARIES
            ],
        ).ask()
    else:
        console.print(f"Using standard vocabularies: {standard_vocabs}")
        selected_standard_vocabularies = standard_vocabs

    # Lazy import
    console.print("Preparing mapping datasets...")
    from aatm.local_database_utils import build_mapping_datasets

    build_mapping_datasets(selected_standard_vocabularies)

    # Lazy import
    console.print("Preparing vector database builder...")
    from aatm.local_database_utils import build_local_vector_database

    build_local_vector_database(
        selected_embedding_model, embedding_dtype=embedding_dtype, vector_db=vector_db
    )
    console.print("[green]Done![/green]\n")

docs.text:
Build the command that starts the Streamlit search UI.

Streamlit's file watcher is disabled by default. It only reloads the app when its source files change, which is not needed to use the UI, and while scanning loaded modules it trips over transformers' lazily loaded submodules, flooding the log with ModuleNotFoundError tracebacks (e.g. "No module named 'torchvision'"). Set STREAMLIT_SERVER_FILE_WATCHER_TYPE (e.g. to auto) to keep Streamlit's own behaviour, for example while developing search_ui.py.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default streamlit_app Path

Path to the Streamlit script.

required env Optional[dict[str, str]]

Environment to check for a user-defined watcher setting. Defaults to os.environ.

None

Returns:

Type Description List[str]

The command as a list of arguments.

Source code in aatm/main.py 
def build_search_ui_command(
    streamlit_app: Path, env: Optional[dict[str, str]] = None
) -> List[str]:
    """Build the command that starts the Streamlit search UI.

    Streamlit's file watcher is disabled by default. It only reloads the app when its
    source files change, which is not needed to use the UI, and while scanning loaded
    modules it trips over `transformers`' lazily loaded submodules, flooding the log
    with `ModuleNotFoundError` tracebacks (e.g. "No module named 'torchvision'").
    Set `STREAMLIT_SERVER_FILE_WATCHER_TYPE` (e.g. to `auto`) to keep Streamlit's
    own behaviour, for example while developing `search_ui.py`.

    Args:
        streamlit_app: Path to the Streamlit script.
        env: Environment to check for a user-defined watcher setting. Defaults to
            `os.environ`.

    Returns:
        The command as a list of arguments.
    """
    env = dict(os.environ) if env is None else env
    command = [sys.executable, "-m", "streamlit", "run", str(streamlit_app)]
    if not env.get(STREAMLIT_FILE_WATCHER_ENV_VAR):
        command += ["--server.fileWatcherType", "none"]
    return command

@app.command("search-ui")

    """Launch the Streamlit-based search interface.

    This command locates the `search_ui.py` application in the same

This command executes a terminology mapping workflow using either a configuration file or parameters provided directly through the command line. When a task configuration file is given, it is loaded and used to build the mapping task. Otherwise, a TerminologyMappingTask is created from the individual command options.

The command prints the loaded task configuration, instantiates a TerminologyMapper from it, and starts the mapping process.

            "--limit-to",
            "-l",
            help="Limit the number of source concepts to map. Useful for testing and debugging.",
        ),
    ] = None,
) -> None:
    """Run a terminology mapping task.

    This command executes a terminology mapping workflow using either a
    configuration file or parameters provided directly through the command
    line. When a task configuration file is given, it is loaded and used to
    build the mapping task. Otherwise, a `TerminologyMappingTask` is created
    from the individual command options.

    The command prints the loaded task configuration, instantiates a
    `TerminologyMapper` from it, and starts the mapping process.

    Args:
        task_config_path (Optional[str]): Path to a task configuration file.
            When provided, the mapping task is loaded from this file.
        input_file (Optional[str]): Path to the input file containing source
            concepts to be mapped. Used when no task configuration file is
            provided.
        output_dir (Optional[str]): Path to the output directory where
            mapping results will be written. Used when no task configuration
            file is provided.
        translator_id (Optional[str]): Identifier of the translator to use
            in the mapping pipeline.
        retriever_id (Optional[str]): Identifier of the retriever to use in
            the mapping pipeline.
        selector_id (Optional[str]): Identifier of the selector to use in
            the mapping pipeline.
        reranker_id (Optional[str]): Identifier of the reranker to use in
            the mapping pipeline.
        batch_size (Optional[int]): Batch size to use during the mapping
            process.
        rate_limit (Optional[int]): Rate limit to apply when processing
            source concepts.
        limit_to (Optional[int]): Maximum number of source concepts to map.
            Useful for testing and debugging.

    Raises:
        typer.Exit: If `task_config_path` is provided but does not exist.

    Examples:
        Run a mapping task from a config file:

            $ aatm map --task-config-path config.yaml

        Run a mapping task from explicit options:

            $ aatm map --input-file concepts.csv --output-dir outputs \\
                --translator-id my_translator --retriever-id my_retriever \\
                --selector-id my_selector

        Run a small test mapping job:

            $ aatm map --input-file concepts.csv --output-dir outputs \\
                --limit-to 20
    """

    # Lazy import
    from aatm.terminology_mapper import TerminologyMapper
    from .data_models import TerminologyMappingTask

    if task_config_path is not None:
        task_config_path = Path(task_config_path)
        if not task_config_path.exists():
            console.print(
                f"[yellow]OOPS![/yellow] You specified a non-existent task config file: `{task_config_path}`. Please, check the path and try again.\n"
            )
            raise typer.Exit()

        task_config = TerminologyMappingTask.from_config_file(task_config_path)
    else:
        if input_file is None or output_dir is None:
            console.print(
                "[yellow]OOPS![/yellow] You must provide both `input_file` when not using a task config file.\n"
            )
            raise typer.Exit()
        task_config = TerminologyMappingTask(
            input_file=input_file,
            output_dir=output_dir,
            translator_id=translator_id,
            retriever_id=retriever_id,
            selector_id=selector_id,
            reranker_id=reranker_id,
            batch_size=batch_size,
            rate_limit=rate_limit,
            limit_to=limit_to,
        )

    print_logo()

    logger.debug(f"Loaded task config: {task_config} {task_config.model_dump()}")

    console.print("[blue]Loaded mapping task config:[/blue]")
    console.print(JSON(task_config.model_dump_json()), "\n")

    console.print("[blue]Started mapping...[/blue]")
    terminology_mapper = TerminologyMapper.from_task_config(task_config)
    terminology_mapper.map()

    console.print("[green]Done![/green]\n")

This command validates the serving configuration, persists the API settings to disk, and launches the FastAPI application using the appropriate runtime mode. It supports development and production execution, optional hot reload, worker configuration, and request-processing parameters such as rate limits and batch size.

Source code in aatm/main.py 
@app.command("serve", help="Serve a FastAPI application with AATM's functionality")
def serve(
    host: Annotated[
        str,
        typer.Option(
            "--host",
            "-h",
            help="Host",
        ),
    ] = "0.0.0.0",
    port: Annotated[
        str,
        typer.Option(
            "--port",
            "-p",
            help="Port",
        ),
    ] = "8000",
    mode: Annotated[
        Literal["prod", "dev"],
        typer.Option("--mode", "-m", help="Serving mode: 'prod' or 'dev'"),
    ] = "dev",
    reload: Annotated[
        bool,
        typer.Option(
            "--reload", help="Enables hot reload. Compatible with 'dev' mode only."
        ),
    ] = False,
    workers: Annotated[
        Optional[int],
        typer.Option(
            "--workers",
            "-w",
            help="Number of workers",
        ),
    ] = None,
    rate_limit: Annotated[
        Optional[int],
        typer.Option(
            "--rate-limit",
            "-r",
            help="Maximum number of documents allowed per minute",
        ),
    ] = None,
    batch_size: Annotated[
        int,
        typer.Option(
            "--batch-size",
            "-b",
            help="Batch size",
        ),
    ] = 100,
) -> None:
    """Serve a FastAPI application exposing AATM functionality.

    This command validates the serving configuration, persists the API settings to
    disk, and launches the FastAPI application using the appropriate runtime mode.
    It supports development and production execution, optional hot reload, worker
    configuration, and request-processing parameters such as rate limits and batch
    size.

    Args:
        host: Host interface on which the FastAPI application will listen.
        port: Port on which the FastAPI application will listen.
        mode: Serving mode. Use `"dev"` for development and `"prod"` for
            production.
        reload: Whether to enable hot reload. This option is only effective in
            development mode.
        workers: Number of worker processes to use. This option is only effective
            in production mode.
        rate_limit: Maximum number of documents allowed per minute.
        batch_size: Batch size used by the API processing pipeline.

    Returns:
        None.

    Raises:
        typer.BadParameter: If the FastAPI application entrypoint cannot be found.
        subprocess.CalledProcessError: If the FastAPI process exits with a
            non-zero status.
    """
    api_main_file = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / Path("api/main.py")

    if not api_main_file.exists():
        raise typer.BadParameter(
            f"FastAPI application implementation was not found: {api_main_file}"
        )

    if reload and mode != "dev":
        console.print(
            f"[yellow]Attention:[/yellow] You provided the flag '--reload' and the mode '{mode}'. Hot reload is only enabled in 'dev' mode, so it will be ignored.\n"
        )

    print_logo()

    # Lazy import
    from aatm.api.config import APIConfig

    # Save API configuration to disk
    api_config = APIConfig(
        host=host,
        port=port,
        rate_limit=rate_limit,
        batch_size=batch_size,
        workers=workers,
    )
    api_config.save_to_disk()

    command = [
        sys.executable,
        "-m",
        "fastapi",
        "run" if mode == "prod" else "dev",
        # default entrypoint is defined at pyproject.toml
        "--host",
        host,
        "--port",
        port,
    ]

    if workers and mode != "prod":
        console.print(
            f"[yellow]Attention:[/yellow] You provided the flag '--workers' and the mode '{mode}'. Workers are only enabled in 'prod' mode, so it will be ignored.\n"
        )
    elif workers:
        command.append("--workers")
        command.append(str(workers))

    if reload and mode == "dev":
        command.append("--reload")

    subprocess.run(
        command,
        check=True,
    )

Diagnose GPU support for local models.

Compares the NVIDIA driver (via nvidia-smi) with the installed PyTorch build and prints the commands that enable GPU acceleration. It does not change the environment.

With code 1 when an action is needed to enable the GPU.

@app.command(
    "doctor",
    help="Check whether local models can use a GPU, and print how to enable it.",
)
def doctor() -> None:
    """Diagnose GPU support for local models.

    Compares the NVIDIA driver (via ``nvidia-smi``) with the installed PyTorch
    build and prints the commands that enable GPU acceleration. It does not
    change the environment.

    Raises:
        typer.Exit: With code 1 when an action is needed to enable the GPU.
    """
    from rich.table import Table

    from aatm.device import DEVICE_ENV_VAR, get_device
    from aatm.doctor import collect_driver_info, collect_torch_info, diagnose

    driver = collect_driver_info()
    torch_info = collect_torch_info()

    table = Table(show_header=False, box=None, padding=(0, 2))
    table.add_column(style="bold", no_wrap=True)
    table.add_column(overflow="fold")
    table.add_row("Python", sys.executable)
    table.add_row(
        "PyTorch",
        f"{torch_info.version} "
        + (f"(CUDA {torch_info.cuda})" if torch_info.cuda else "(CPU-only build)"),
    )
    if driver is None:
        table.add_row("NVIDIA driver", "not found")
    else:
        max_cuda = (
            f"{driver.max_cuda[0]}.{driver.max_cuda[1]}" if driver.max_cuda else "?"
        )
        table.add_row("NVIDIA GPU", driver.gpu_name or "unknown")
        table.add_row(
            "NVIDIA driver",
            f"{driver.driver_version or 'unknown'} (supports CUDA up to {max_cuda})",
        )
    try:
        device_label: str = get_device()
    except ValueError as e:
        device_label = f"error: {e}"
    table.add_row("AATM device", device_label)
    if os.environ.get(DEVICE_ENV_VAR):
        table.add_row(DEVICE_ENV_VAR, os.environ[DEVICE_ENV_VAR])

    console.print(table)
    console.print()

    diagnosis = diagnose(driver, torch_info)
    style = {"ok": "green", "info": "blue", "action": "yellow"}[diagnosis.status]
    console.print(f"[bold {style}]{diagnosis.summary}[/bold {style}]")
    for line in diagnosis.details:
        console.print(line)
    if diagnosis.commands:
        console.print()
        for command in diagnosis.commands:
            # Print commands verbatim (no markup, no wrapping) so they can be copied.
            console.print(command, markup=False, highlight=False, soft_wrap=True)

    if diagnosis.status == "action":
        raise typer.Exit(code=1)

docs.text:
Print the configured vector database and, remotely, its collections or indexes.

Raises:

Type Description Exit

With code 1 if the configuration is invalid or the connection fails.

Source code in aatm/main.py 
@vector_db_app.command(
    "check", help="Show where the vector database lives and test the connection"
)
def vector_db_check(
    vector_db: Annotated[
        Optional[str],
        typer.Option(
            "--vector-db",
            help="'local', 'cloud' or 'pinecone'. Overrides AATM_VECTOR_DB.",
        ),
    ] = None,
) -> None:
    """Print the configured vector database and, remotely, its collections or indexes.

    Raises:
        typer.Exit: With code 1 if the configuration is invalid or the
            connection fails.
    """
    from aatm.registries.retrievers import CHROMADB_RETRIEVER_MODEL_REGISTRY
    from aatm.vector_db import VectorDatabaseConfigError, resolve_vector_db_mode

    try:
        mode = resolve_vector_db_mode(vector_db)
        locations = {
            name: spec.vector_db_location(mode)
            for name, spec in CHROMADB_RETRIEVER_MODEL_REGISTRY.items()
        }
    except VectorDatabaseConfigError as e:
        console.print(f"[yellow]OOPS![/yellow] {e}")
        raise typer.Exit(code=1)

    if mode == "local":
        console.print("Vector database: [bold]local[/bold]")
        for name, (connection, collection_name) in locations.items():
            path = getattr(connection, "path", None)
            status = (
                "[green]built[/green]" if path and Path(path).exists() else "not built"
            )
            console.print(f"  {name}: {path} ({status})")
        return

    connection = next(iter(locations.values()))[0]
    console.print(f"Vector database: [bold]{connection.describe()}[/bold]")
    service = "Pinecone" if mode == "pinecone" else "Chroma Cloud"
    kind = "index" if mode == "pinecone" else "collection"
    try:
        client = connection.client()
        if mode == "pinecone":
            existing = set(client.list_indexes().names())
        else:
            existing = {collection.name for collection in client.list_collections()}
    except VectorDatabaseConfigError as e:
        console.print(f"[yellow]OOPS![/yellow] {e}")
        raise typer.Exit(code=1)
    except Exception as e:
        console.print(f"[red]Could not connect to {service}:[/red] {e}")
        raise typer.Exit(code=1)

    console.print("[green]Connected.[/green]")
    for name, (_, collection_name) in locations.items():
        status = "[green]built[/green]" if collection_name in existing else "not built"
        console.print(f"  {name}: {kind} '{collection_name}' ({status})")

docs.text:
Upload a local index to Chroma Cloud or Pinecone. Re-running resumes where it stopped.

Raises:

Type Description Exit

With code 1 if the model is unknown, the local database is missing, or the cloud configuration is invalid.

Source code in aatm/main.py 
@vector_db_app.command(
    "upload",
    help="Copy a local vector database to Chroma Cloud or Pinecone without re-embedding",
)
def vector_db_upload(
    embedding_model: Annotated[
        str,
        typer.Option(
            "--embedding-model",
            "-e",
            help="Name of the embedding model whose index to upload.",
        ),
    ],
    local_dir: Annotated[
        Optional[Path],
        typer.Option(
            "--local-dir",
            help="Local vector database directory. Defaults to the model's path "
            "under .aatm/chroma_vector_dbs.",
            show_default=False,
        ),
    ] = None,
    batch_size: Annotated[
        Optional[int],
        typer.Option(
            "--batch-size",
            help=(
                "Rows per write. Capped at Chroma Cloud's maximum batch size; "
                "split into requests within Pinecone's limits."
            ),
            show_default=False,
        ),
    ] = None,
    to: Annotated[
        str,
        typer.Option(
            "--to",
            help="Destination: 'cloud' (Chroma Cloud) or 'pinecone'.",
        ),
    ] = "cloud",
    ids_file: Annotated[
        Optional[Path],
        typer.Option(
            "--ids-file",
            help=(
                "Only upload the rows whose IDs this file lists, one per line, "
                "e.g. a subset that fits a free plan."
            ),
            show_default=False,
        ),
    ] = None,
) -> None:
    """Upload a local index to Chroma Cloud or Pinecone. Re-running resumes where it stopped.

    Raises:
        typer.Exit: With code 1 if the model is unknown, the local database is
            missing, or the cloud configuration is invalid.
    """
    if embedding_model not in SUPPORTED_EMBEDDING_MODELS:
        console.print(
            f"[yellow]OOPS![/yellow] Unsupported embedding model: `{embedding_model}`. "
            f"The supported embedding models are: {SUPPORTED_EMBEDDING_MODELS}"
        )
        raise typer.Exit(code=1)

    from aatm.local_database_utils import upload_vector_database_to_cloud

    ids = None
    if ids_file is not None:
        if not ids_file.exists():
            console.print(f"[yellow]OOPS![/yellow] No IDs file at '{ids_file}'.")
            raise typer.Exit(code=1)
        ids = [
            line.strip() for line in ids_file.read_text().splitlines() if line.strip()
        ]

    try:
        upload_vector_database_to_cloud(
            embedding_model,
            vector_db_dir=local_dir,
            write_batch_size=batch_size,
            to=to.strip().lower(),
            ids=ids,
        )
    except ValueError as e:
        console.print(f"[yellow]OOPS![/yellow] {e}")
        raise typer.Exit(code=1)

@cache_app.command("info", help="Show the entries, size and coders of the cache")
def cache_info(path: CachePathOption = Path(".aatm/coding_cache.db")) -> None:
    """Print the number of entries, their size and the coder identities they belong to."""
    from rich.table import Table

    info = _open_cache(path).info()
    console.print(
        f"{info.path}: {info.entries} entries, {_size(info.bytes)} of results, "
        f"{_size(info.file_bytes)} on disk"
    )
    if not info.coders:
        return
    table = Table("Coder", "Entries", "Identity")
    for coder in info.coders:
        identity = coder.identity.get("identity", {})
        label = identity.get("coder", "?") if isinstance(identity, dict) else "?"
        table.add_row(
            coder.coder,
            str(coder.entries),
            f"{label}, aatm {coder.identity.get('aatm')}",
        )
    console.print(table)

    cache = _open_cache(path)
    what = f"the entries of coder {coder}" if coder else f"all {len(cache)} entries"
    if not yes and not typer.confirm(f"Delete {what} from {path}?"):
        raise typer.Exit()
    removed = cache.clear(coder)
    console.print(f"Deleted {removed} entries from {path}")

docs.text:
Agentic concept search: an LLM agent that searches the vocabularies for the right code.

One retrieval on a short span often misses the right concept. ConceptSearchAgent gets the text and its context and searches with tools (semantic search, lexical search, code lookup, concept details, hierarchy) until it finds the standard concept or concludes there is none. It is available in both pipelines:

  • Notes to OMOP tables: OmopTableBuilder(definitions, mapper=AgenticCoder(...)) (aatm.omop.AgenticCoder). The builder passes each text's related values and note line.
  • Terminology mapping: TerminologyMapper(selector=AgenticSelector(...)). The agent starts from the mapper's retrieved candidates, with each source concept's code and vocabulary as context.

See aatm.concept_search.agent for the confidence scale of the scores.

An LLM agent that searches the vocabularies for the standard concept of a text.

A single retrieval on a short span often misses the right concept: "creatinine" says nothing of the specimen, and "Hb" or "potássio" need expanding or translating before an embedding search finds them. The agent gets the text and its context (related values such as the unit, the sentence of the note, the target column) and searches iteratively with tools until it finds the concept or concludes there is none:

from aatm.concept_search import CodingContext, ConceptSearchAgent, ConceptSearchTools
from aatm.registries.retrievers import load_retriever

agent = ConceptSearchAgent(
    "openai/gpt-5-mini",
    ConceptSearchTools(load_retriever("text-embedding-3-small"), vocabulary=".aatm/omop.db"),
)
context = CodingContext(text="creatinine", related={"unit": "mg/dl", "value": "1.4"})
result = await agent.search(context, domain="Measurement")
result.concept, result.score, result.rationale, result.trace

The agent is used by aatm.omop.AgenticCoder (extraction to OMOP tables) and by aatm.concept_search.AgenticSelector (terminology mapping with TerminologyMapper).

The loop is provider-agnostic: at each step the model answers with one structured AgentStep (an action and its arguments), so any aatm.llm model works, without native tool calling.

The tools the concept search agent calls to explore the vocabularies.

  • Semantic search over the vector index (ChromaDB or Pinecone) of a retriever, filtered by domain and vocabulary.
  • Lexical search: concept names and synonyms containing every word of a query, in the local vocabulary database (.aatm/omop.db).
  • Code lookup: a code in any vocabulary, with the standard concepts it maps to.
  • Concept details: domain, standard status, synonyms, "Maps to" and, for LOINC, the axes of the code (component, property, time, system, scale, method).
  • Hierarchy: the direct parents or children of a standard concept.

Every tool except concept details only returns standard concepts within the search scope (domain and vocabularies), so whatever the agent picks from its results is a valid answer.

The concept search agent as a selector of the terminology-mapping pipeline.

AgenticSelector replaces the selector of a aatm.terminology_mapper.TerminologyMapper. It starts from the candidates the mapper's retriever (and reranker) found, and the agent searches further when none of them fits:

from aatm.concept_search import AgenticSelector
from aatm.terminology_mapper import TerminologyMapper

mapper = TerminologyMapper(
    retriever="text-embedding-3-small",
    selector=AgenticSelector("openai/gpt-5-mini"),
)
df = mapper.map(file_path="source_concepts.csv")
df[["source_code_description", "target_concept_id", "confidence_score", "mapping_rationale"]]

The selector uses the mapper's retriever for its own searches, and the vocabulary database built by aatm init (.aatm/omop.db) for lexical search, code lookups, concept details and hierarchy. For source concepts, the source code and vocabulary are given to the agent as context.

class AgentStep(BaseModel):
    """One step of the agent: the next action and its arguments.

    Every field is required (``null`` when unused) so the schema is accepted by
    every provider's structured-output mode.
    """

    reasoning: str = Field(
        description="One or two sentences: what the last results showed and why "
        "this action is next."
    )
    action: Action
    query: Optional[str] = Field(
        description="Search text for semantic_search and lexical_search, or the "
        "code for code_lookup. null otherwise."
    )
    concept_id: Optional[int] = Field(
        description="Concept id for concept_details, hierarchy and finish. null "
        "otherwise, or for finish when no concept fits."
    )
    direction: Optional[Literal["parents", "children"]] = Field(
        description="For hierarchy: parents (more general) or children (more "
        "specific). null otherwise."
    )
    confidence: Optional[Confidence] = Field(
        description="For finish: high, medium or low (see the scale). null otherwise."
    )

class CodingContext(BaseModel):
    """A text to code and what is known around it.

    Attributes:
        text: The text to code, e.g. ``"creatinine"``.
        related: Related values, e.g. ``{"lab_value": "1.4", "lab_unit": "mg/dl"}``
            from the children of an extracted mention, or ``{"source_code": "I63"}``
            for a source concept.
        sentence: The sentence or line of the note the text comes from.
        target: What the concept is for, e.g. ``"measurement.measurement_concept_id"``.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    text: str
    related: dict[str, str] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    sentence: Optional[str] = None
    target: Optional[str] = None

    def cache_key(self) -> str:
        """Identical contexts share a key, so they are searched once."""
        return json.dumps(self.model_dump(), sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False)

    def describe(self) -> str:
        lines = [f"Text to code: {self.text!r}"]
        if self.related:
            lines.append(
                "Related values: "
                + "; ".join(f"{k}={v!r}" for k, v in self.related.items())
            )
        if self.sentence and self.sentence.strip() != self.text:
            lines.append(f"Sentence: {self.sentence.strip()!r}")
        if self.target:
            lines.append(f"Target: {self.target}")
        return "\n".join(lines)

class ConceptSearchAgent:
    """Searches the vocabularies for the standard concept of a text, with tools.

    Args:
        model: An `aatm.llm` model id such as ``"openai/gpt-5-mini"``, or a
            `aatm.llm.StructuredLLM`.
        tools: The search tools.
        max_tool_calls: Tool calls the agent may make per text, after the initial
            semantic search. When they run out, the agent must answer with what it
            has seen, and its confidence is capped at ``low``.
        settings: Generation settings for a model given by id. For more
            reproducible runs, set ``temperature=0`` on models that accept it
            (reasoning models such as GPT-5 reject it); the trace makes runs
            comparable either way.
        top_k: Results per search.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        model: str | StructuredLLM,
        tools: ConceptSearchTools,
        max_tool_calls: int = 8,
        settings: Optional[LLMSettings | dict[str, Any]] = None,
        top_k: int = 10,
    ):
        if max_tool_calls < 0:
            raise ValueError("max_tool_calls must be >= 0")
        if isinstance(model, str):
            model = create_llm(model, settings=settings)
        self.llm: StructuredLLM = model
        self.tools = tools
        self.max_tool_calls = max_tool_calls
        self.top_k = top_k

    async def search(
        self,
        context: CodingContext,
        domain: Optional[str] = None,
        vocabularies: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None,
        initial_candidates: Optional[Sequence[Candidate]] = None,
    ) -> ConceptSearchResult:
        """Find the standard concept of `context.text` within a domain and vocabularies.

        Args:
            context: The text and its context.
            domain: Only concepts of this domain qualify.
            vocabularies: Only concepts of these vocabularies qualify.
            initial_candidates: Candidates already retrieved for the text, e.g. by a
                `TerminologyMapper`. When ``None``, the agent starts with a semantic
                search on the text (or a lexical search without a retriever).

        Returns:
            The result. Errors from the model are caught and reported in
            ``error``, with no concept.
        """
        start = time.perf_counter()
        result = ConceptSearchResult()
        with track_usage() as usage:
            try:
                await self._run(
                    context, domain, vocabularies, initial_candidates, result
                )
            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - one text must not stop a batch
                logger.warning("Concept search failed for %r: %s", context.text, e)
                result.concept = None
                result.confidence = None
                result.score = None
                result.error = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
                result.rationale = f"Search failed: {result.error}"
        result.llm_calls = usage.calls
        result.input_tokens = usage.input_tokens
        result.output_tokens = usage.output_tokens
        result.seconds = time.perf_counter() - start
        return result

    async def _run(
        self,
        context: CodingContext,
        domain: Optional[str],
        vocabularies: Optional[Sequence[str]],
        initial_candidates: Optional[Sequence[Candidate]],
        result: ConceptSearchResult,
    ) -> None:
        seen: dict[int, Candidate] = {}
        history: list[str] = []

        def observe(candidates: Sequence[Candidate]) -> str:
            for c in candidates:
                if c.standard is not False and in_scope(c, domain, vocabularies):
                    seen.setdefault(c.concept_id, c)
            if not candidates:
                return "No results."
            return "\n".join(c.line() for c in candidates)

        # Step 0: the candidates of a plain retrieval, so easy texts need one LLM call.
        if initial_candidates is not None:
            first = list(initial_candidates)
            label = f"retrieved candidates for {context.text!r}"
            result.trace.append(
                {"action": "retrieved", "results": [c.short() for c in first]}
            )
        else:
            action = (
                "semantic_search"
                if self.tools.retriever is not None
                else "lexical_search"
            )
            first = await self._tool(action, context.text, domain, vocabularies)
            result.tool_calls += 1
            label = f"{action} {context.text!r}"
            result.trace.append(
                {
                    "action": action,
                    "query": context.text,
                    "results": [c.short() for c in first],
                }
            )
        history.append(f"[{label}]\n{observe(first)}")

        system = SYSTEM_PROMPT.format(
            scope=_scope_text(domain, vocabularies),
            actions="\n".join(ACTION_HELP[a] for a in self.tools.actions),
        )
        calls_left = self.max_tool_calls
        retries_left = 2  # invalid finishes or unavailable actions
        while True:
            forced = calls_left <= 0
            user = self._prompt(context, history, calls_left)
            step = await self.llm.generate(
                system=system, user=user, output_type=AgentStep
            )
            entry: dict[str, Any] = {"action": step.action, "reasoning": step.reasoning}

            if step.action == "finish" or forced:
                if step.action != "finish":
                    # The model ignored the instruction to finish: take nothing.
                    entry["error"] = "budget exhausted"
                    result.trace.append(entry)
                    result.budget_exhausted = True
                    result.rationale = "Tool budget exhausted before an answer."
                    return
                entry.update(concept_id=step.concept_id, confidence=step.confidence)
                problem = self._finish(step, seen, domain, vocabularies, result)
                if problem is None:
                    if forced:
                        result.budget_exhausted = True
                        if result.concept is not None:
                            result.confidence = "low"
                            result.score = CONFIDENCE_SCORES["low"]
                    result.trace.append(entry)
                    return
                entry["error"] = problem
                result.trace.append(entry)
                if forced or retries_left == 0:
                    result.concept = None
                    result.confidence = result.score = None
                    result.budget_exhausted = forced
                    result.rationale = f"No valid answer: {problem}"
                    return
                retries_left -= 1
                history.append(f"[finish {step.concept_id}]\nRejected: {problem}")
                continue

            if step.action not in self.tools.actions:
                problem = f"{step.action} is not available. Use one of {self.tools.actions} or finish."
            else:
                problem = self._missing_argument(step)
            if problem is not None:
                entry["error"] = problem
                result.trace.append(entry)
                if retries_left == 0:
                    result.rationale = f"No valid answer: {problem}"
                    return
                retries_left -= 1
                history.append(f"[{step.action}]\nError: {problem}")
                continue

            calls_left -= 1
            result.tool_calls += 1
            label, observation, summary = await self._execute(
                step, domain, vocabularies, observe
            )
            entry.update(summary)
            result.trace.append(entry)
            history.append(f"[{label}]\n{observation}")

    @staticmethod
    def _missing_argument(step: AgentStep) -> Optional[str]:
        if step.action in ("semantic_search", "lexical_search", "code_lookup"):
            if not (step.query or "").strip():
                return f"{step.action} needs a query."
        if step.action in ("concept_details", "hierarchy") and step.concept_id is None:
            return f"{step.action} needs a concept_id."
        if step.action == "hierarchy" and step.direction is None:
            return "hierarchy needs a direction: parents or children."
        return None

    async def _tool(
        self,
        action: str,
        query: str,
        domain: Optional[str],
        vocabularies: Optional[Sequence[str]],
    ) -> list[Candidate]:
        method = getattr(self.tools, action)
        # The tools block (SQLite, the vector database): run them off the event loop.
        return await asyncio.to_thread(method, query, domain, vocabularies, self.top_k)

    async def _execute(
        self,
        step: AgentStep,
        domain: Optional[str],
        vocabularies: Optional[Sequence[str]],
        observe: Any,
    ) -> tuple[str, str, dict[str, Any]]:
        if step.action in ("semantic_search", "lexical_search"):
            query = step.query.strip()  # type: ignore[union-attr]
            found = await self._tool(step.action, query, domain, vocabularies)
            return (
                f"{step.action} {query!r}",
                observe(found),
                {"query": query, "results": [c.short() for c in found]},
            )
        if step.action == "code_lookup":
            code = step.query.strip()  # type: ignore[union-attr]
            found = await asyncio.to_thread(
                self.tools.code_lookup, code, domain, vocabularies
            )
            return (
                f"code_lookup {code!r}",
                observe(found),
                {"query": code, "results": [c.short() for c in found]},
            )
        if step.action == "concept_details":
            assert step.concept_id is not None  # checked by _missing_argument
            details = await asyncio.to_thread(
                self.tools.concept_details, step.concept_id
            )
            return (
                f"concept_details {step.concept_id}",
                details,
                {"concept_id": step.concept_id},
            )
        assert step.action == "hierarchy"
        # Checked by _missing_argument.
        assert step.concept_id is not None and step.direction is not None
        found = await asyncio.to_thread(
            self.tools.hierarchy,
            step.concept_id,
            step.direction,
            domain,
            vocabularies,
            self.top_k,
        )
        return (
            f"hierarchy {step.direction} of {step.concept_id}",
            observe(found),
            {
                "concept_id": step.concept_id,
                "direction": step.direction,
                "results": [c.short() for c in found],
            },
        )

    def _finish(
        self,
        step: AgentStep,
        seen: dict[int, Candidate],
        domain: Optional[str],
        vocabularies: Optional[Sequence[str]],
        result: ConceptSearchResult,
    ) -> Optional[str]:
        """Record a finish step; return why it is rejected, or ``None``."""
        result.rationale = step.reasoning
        if step.concept_id is None:
            result.concept = None
            result.confidence = result.score = None
            return None
        if step.confidence is None:
            return "finish with a concept needs a confidence: high, medium or low."
        candidate = seen.get(step.concept_id)
        if candidate is None:
            # Not returned in scope by a tool: accept it only if the vocabulary
            # confirms it qualifies.
            vocabulary = self.tools.vocabulary
            concept = (
                vocabulary.by_id([step.concept_id]).get(step.concept_id)
                if vocabulary is not None
                else None
            )
            if concept is None or not in_scope(concept, domain, vocabularies):
                return (
                    f"{step.concept_id} is not a standard concept "
                    f"{_scope_text(domain, vocabularies)} returned by a tool."
                )
            candidate = Candidate.from_concept(concept)
        result.concept = candidate
        result.confidence = step.confidence
        result.score = CONFIDENCE_SCORES[step.confidence]
        return None

    @staticmethod
    def _prompt(context: CodingContext, history: list[str], calls_left: int) -> str:
        budget = (
            f"Tool calls left: {calls_left}."
            if calls_left > 0
            else "No tool calls left: you must finish now, with a concept from the "
            "results above or null."
        )
        return (
            f"{context.describe()}\n\n"
            "Results so far:\n\n"
            + "\n\n".join(history)
            + f"\n\n{budget} Choose the next action."
        )

    async def search_many(
        self,
        items: Sequence[tuple[CodingContext, Optional[Sequence[Candidate]]]],
        domain: Optional[str] = None,
        vocabularies: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None,
        max_concurrency: int = 8,
    ) -> list[ConceptSearchResult]:
        """Search several texts concurrently; identical contexts are searched once.

        Args:
            items: ``(context, initial_candidates)`` pairs.
            domain: See `search`.
            vocabularies: See `search`.
            max_concurrency: Searches running at the same time.

        Returns:
            One result per item, in order.
        """
        semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(max_concurrency)
        unique: dict[str, tuple[CodingContext, Optional[Sequence[Candidate]]]] = {}
        for context, initial in items:
            unique.setdefault(context.cache_key(), (context, initial))

        async def run(context: CodingContext, initial: Any) -> ConceptSearchResult:
            async with semaphore:
                return await self.search(context, domain, vocabularies, initial)

        keys = list(unique)
        results = await asyncio.gather(*(run(*unique[k]) for k in keys))
        by_key = dict(zip(keys, results))
        return [by_key[context.cache_key()] for context, _ in items]

class Candidate(BaseModel):
    """A concept returned by a tool.

    Attributes:
        concept_id: The concept's id.
        concept_name: Its name.
        vocabulary_id: Its vocabulary.
        concept_code: Its code in that vocabulary.
        domain_id: Its domain.
        standard: Whether it is a standard concept.
        matched: The indexed text that matched a semantic search, when it is not the
            concept name (a synonym, or the name of a concept that maps to it).
    """

    concept_id: int
    concept_name: str
    vocabulary_id: str
    concept_code: str
    domain_id: str
    standard: Optional[bool] = None
    matched: Optional[str] = None

    @classmethod
    def from_concept(cls, concept: Concept) -> "Candidate":
        return cls(
            concept_id=concept.concept_id,
            concept_name=concept.concept_name,
            vocabulary_id=concept.vocabulary_id,
            concept_code=concept.concept_code,
            domain_id=concept.domain_id,
            standard=concept.is_standard,
        )

    def line(self) -> str:
        """One line for the agent's prompt."""
        text = (
            f"{self.concept_id} | {self.vocabulary_id} {self.concept_code} | "
            f"{self.concept_name} | {self.domain_id}"
        )
        if self.standard is False:
            text += " | non-standard"
        if self.matched and self.matched.casefold() != self.concept_name.casefold():
            text += f" | matched: {self.matched!r}"
        return text

    def short(self) -> str:
        """``id name``, for traces."""
        return f"{self.concept_id} {self.concept_name}"

class ConceptSearchTools:
    """The agent's tools over a retriever and a vocabulary database.

    Args:
        retriever: A retriever with a ``retrieve(queries, where=..., top_k=...)``
            method, such as `aatm.retrievers.ChromaDBRetriever` or
            `aatm.retrievers.PineconeRetriever`, for semantic search.
        vocabulary: The vocabulary database, as a path or a `VocabularySearch`, for
            lexical search, code lookup, concept details and hierarchy. ``None``
            leaves only semantic search.
        top_k: Number of results per search.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        retriever: Any = None,
        vocabulary: VocabularySearch | str | Path | None = None,
        top_k: int = 10,
    ):
        if retriever is None and vocabulary is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "The concept search needs a retriever, a vocabulary, or both"
            )
        self.retriever = retriever
        self.vocabulary = (
            VocabularySearch(vocabulary)
            if isinstance(vocabulary, (str, Path))
            else vocabulary
        )
        self.top_k = top_k

    @property
    def actions(self) -> list[str]:
        """The tools available with this configuration."""
        actions = []
        if self.retriever is not None:
            actions.append("semantic_search")
        if self.vocabulary is not None:
            actions += ["lexical_search", "code_lookup", "concept_details", "hierarchy"]
        return actions

    def semantic_search(
        self,
        query: str,
        domain: Optional[str] = None,
        vocabularies: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None,
        top_k: Optional[int] = None,
    ) -> list[Candidate]:
        if self.retriever is None:
            raise ValueError("semantic_search needs a retriever")
        k = top_k or self.top_k
        # Several indexed expressions (synonyms) can point to the same concept:
        # retrieve more to return about k distinct concepts.
        results = self.retriever.retrieve(
            [query], where=retriever_filter(domain, vocabularies), top_k=k * 2
        )
        return candidates_from_expressions(results.results[0])[:k]

    def lexical_search(
        self,
        query: str,
        domain: Optional[str] = None,
        vocabularies: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None,
        top_k: Optional[int] = None,
    ) -> list[Candidate]:
        assert self.vocabulary is not None
        return self.vocabulary.search_names(
            query, domain, vocabularies, limit=top_k or self.top_k
        )

    def code_lookup(
        self,
        code: str,
        domain: Optional[str] = None,
        vocabularies: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None,
    ) -> list[Candidate]:
        """The concepts with this code, and the in-scope standard concepts they map to."""
        assert self.vocabulary is not None
        found = self.vocabulary.search_code(code)
        maps_to = self.vocabulary.maps_to(c.concept_id for c in found if not c.standard)
        targets = self.vocabulary.by_id({t for ts in maps_to.values() for t in ts})
        results: list[Candidate] = []
        for candidate in found:
            results.append(candidate)
            for target_id in maps_to.get(candidate.concept_id, []):
                target = targets.get(target_id)
                if target is not None:
                    mapped = Candidate.from_concept(target)
                    mapped.matched = (
                        f"maps from {candidate.vocabulary_id} {candidate.concept_code}"
                    )
                    results.append(mapped)
        return [
            c for c in results if not c.standard or in_scope(c, domain, vocabularies)
        ]

    def concept_details(self, concept_id: int) -> str:
        assert self.vocabulary is not None
        concept = self.vocabulary.by_id([concept_id]).get(concept_id)
        if concept is None:
            return f"No concept with id {concept_id}."
        lines = [
            f"concept_id: {concept.concept_id}",
            f"name: {concept.concept_name}",
            f"vocabulary: {concept.vocabulary_id} {concept.concept_code}",
            f"domain: {concept.domain_id}",
            f"standard: {'yes' if concept.is_standard else 'no'}",
        ]
        if concept.invalid_reason:
            lines.append(f"invalid_reason: {concept.invalid_reason}")
        synonyms = self.vocabulary.synonyms(concept_id)
        if synonyms:
            lines.append(f"synonyms: {'; '.join(synonyms)}")
        relationships = self.vocabulary.relationships(concept_id)
        related_ids = {
            target
            for rel, target in relationships
            if rel in LOINC_AXES or rel == "Maps to"
        }
        names = self.vocabulary.by_id(related_ids)
        axes = {
            LOINC_AXES[rel]: names[target].concept_name
            for rel, target in relationships
            if rel in LOINC_AXES and target in names
        }
        if axes:
            lines.append(
                "LOINC axes: "
                + "; ".join(
                    f"{axis}={axes[axis]}"
                    for axis in LOINC_AXES.values()
                    if axis in axes
                )
            )
        maps_to = [
            names[target]
            for rel, target in relationships
            if rel == "Maps to" and target in names and target != concept_id
        ]
        for target in maps_to:
            lines.append(f"maps to: {Candidate.from_concept(target).line()}")
        return "\n".join(lines)

    def hierarchy(
        self,
        concept_id: int,
        direction: Literal["parents", "children"],
        domain: Optional[str] = None,
        vocabularies: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None,
        top_k: Optional[int] = None,
    ) -> list[Candidate]:
        assert self.vocabulary is not None
        return self.vocabulary.neighbours(
            concept_id, direction, domain, vocabularies, limit=(top_k or self.top_k) * 2
        )

class VocabularySearch(SqliteConceptLookup):
    """Searches in the SQLite vocabulary database built by ``aatm init``.

    The tables are not indexed, so each search scans a table once (well under a
    second for the concept table of a typical download).
    """

    def __init__(self, path: str | Path = DEFAULT_VOCABULARY_DB):
        super().__init__(path)

    @staticmethod
    def _scope_sql(
        domain: Optional[str], vocabularies: Optional[Sequence[str]], alias: str = "c"
    ) -> tuple[str, list]:
        sql = f" AND {alias}.standard_concept = 'S' AND {alias}.invalid_reason IS NULL"
        params: list = []
        if domain is not None:
            sql += f" AND {alias}.domain_id = ?"
            params.append(domain)
        if vocabularies:
            sql += (
                f" AND {alias}.vocabulary_id IN ({','.join('?' * len(vocabularies))})"
            )
            params.extend(vocabularies)
        return sql, params

    def search_names(
        self,
        query: str,
        domain: Optional[str] = None,
        vocabularies: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None,
        limit: int = 20,
    ) -> list[Candidate]:
        """Standard concepts whose name or a synonym contains every word of `query`.

        Ranked by: exact name, name starting with the query, then shorter names, which
        are usually the more general concepts.
        """
        words = [w for w in query.casefold().split() if w]
        if not words:
            return []
        scope, scope_params = self._scope_sql(domain, vocabularies)
        like = " AND ".join("lower({col}) LIKE ?" for _ in words)
        like_params = [f"%{w}%" for w in words]
        rows = self._query(
            "SELECT c.concept_id, c.concept_name, c.domain_id, c.vocabulary_id, "
            "c.concept_code, c.standard_concept, c.invalid_reason, c.concept_name "
            f"FROM concept c WHERE {like.format(col='c.concept_name')}{scope} "
            "UNION "
            "SELECT c.concept_id, c.concept_name, c.domain_id, c.vocabulary_id, "
            "c.concept_code, c.standard_concept, c.invalid_reason, s.concept_synonym_name "
            "FROM concept_synonym s JOIN concept c ON c.concept_id = s.concept_id "
            f"WHERE {like.format(col='s.concept_synonym_name')}{scope}",
            [*like_params, *scope_params, *like_params, *scope_params],
        )
        q = query.casefold().strip()
        best: dict[int, tuple[tuple, Candidate]] = {}
        for row in rows:
            candidate = Candidate.from_concept(self._concept(row[:7]))
            matched = row[7] or candidate.concept_name
            candidate.matched = matched
            m = matched.casefold()
            rank = (0 if m == q else 1 if m.startswith(q) else 2, len(m), m)
            current = best.get(candidate.concept_id)
            if current is None or rank < current[0]:
                best[candidate.concept_id] = (rank, candidate)
        ordered = sorted(best.values(), key=lambda item: item[0])
        return [candidate for _, candidate in ordered[:limit]]

    def search_code(self, code: str) -> list[Candidate]:
        """Concepts of any vocabulary whose code is `code`, ignoring case."""
        code = code.strip()
        if not code:
            return []
        rows = self._query(
            "SELECT concept_id, concept_name, domain_id, vocabulary_id, concept_code, "
            "standard_concept, invalid_reason FROM concept "
            "WHERE lower(concept_code) = ?",
            [code.lower()],
        )
        return [Candidate.from_concept(self._concept(row)) for row in rows]

    def relationships(self, concept_id: int) -> list[tuple[str, int]]:
        """Valid ``(relationship_id, concept_id_2)`` pairs of a concept."""
        rows = self._query(
            "SELECT relationship_id, concept_id_2 FROM concept_relationship "
            "WHERE concept_id_1 = ? AND invalid_reason IS NULL",
            [str(concept_id)],
        )
        return [(rel, int(target)) for rel, target in rows]

    def synonyms(self, concept_id: int, limit: int = 10) -> list[str]:
        rows = self._query(
            "SELECT concept_synonym_name FROM concept_synonym WHERE concept_id = ?",
            [str(concept_id)],
        )
        return sorted({r[0] for r in rows if r[0]})[:limit]

    def neighbours(
        self,
        concept_id: int,
        direction: Literal["parents", "children"],
        domain: Optional[str] = None,
        vocabularies: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None,
        limit: int = 25,
    ) -> list[Candidate]:
        """Direct parents or children of a standard concept (``concept_ancestor``)."""
        this, other = (
            ("descendant", "ancestor")
            if direction == "parents"
            else ("ancestor", "descendant")
        )
        scope, scope_params = self._scope_sql(domain, vocabularies)
        rows = self._query(
            "SELECT c.concept_id, c.concept_name, c.domain_id, c.vocabulary_id, "
            "c.concept_code, c.standard_concept, c.invalid_reason "
            f"FROM concept_ancestor a JOIN concept c ON c.concept_id = a.{other}_concept_id "
            f"WHERE a.{this}_concept_id = ? AND a.min_levels_of_separation = '1'{scope}",
            [str(concept_id), *scope_params],
        )
        candidates = sorted(
            (Candidate.from_concept(self._concept(row)) for row in rows),
            key=lambda c: (len(c.concept_name), c.concept_name),
        )
        return candidates[:limit]

docs.text:
The agent reports a confidence level, stored as a score:

Level Score Meaning high 0.9 The concept matches the text and everything the context states (e.g. specimen and unit). medium 0.6 The right concept, but a detail the context does not state was assumed (e.g. serum for a chemistry test without specimen). low 0.3 The closest concept available, with a known mismatch or real ambiguity.

When the tool budget runs out, the agent must answer with what it has seen, and the score is capped at low. min_score: 0.5 therefore keeps high and medium.

class CodingContext(BaseModel):
    """A text to code and what is known around it.

    Attributes:
        text: The text to code, e.g. ``"creatinine"``.
        related: Related values, e.g. ``{"lab_value": "1.4", "lab_unit": "mg/dl"}``
            from the children of an extracted mention, or ``{"source_code": "I63"}``
            for a source concept.
        sentence: The sentence or line of the note the text comes from.
        target: What the concept is for, e.g. ``"measurement.measurement_concept_id"``.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    text: str
    related: dict[str, str] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    sentence: Optional[str] = None
    target: Optional[str] = None

    def cache_key(self) -> str:
        """Identical contexts share a key, so they are searched once."""
        return json.dumps(self.model_dump(), sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False)

    def describe(self) -> str:
        lines = [f"Text to code: {self.text!r}"]
        if self.related:
            lines.append(
                "Related values: "
                + "; ".join(f"{k}={v!r}" for k, v in self.related.items())
            )
        if self.sentence and self.sentence.strip() != self.text:
            lines.append(f"Sentence: {self.sentence.strip()!r}")
        if self.target:
            lines.append(f"Target: {self.target}")
        return "\n".join(lines)
